bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第189卷卷第一百八十九

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 189, scroll number one hundred eighty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 189, Scroll 189.

sentences.zh: 【唐紀五】起重光大荒落三月，盡十二月，不滿一年。

translations.literal: Tang Records 5: Beginning from the third month of the year Chongguang Dahuangluo, through the twelfth month—less than one full year.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Records 5: From the third month of the year Chongguang Dahuangluo through the twelfth month—less than a full calendar year.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚申，以靺鞨渠帥突地稽為燕州總管。

translations.literal: In the third month, on gengshen, Tumoji, a Mohe chieftain, was appointed regional commander of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day gengshen, the Mohe chieftain Tumoji was made regional commander of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 太子建成獲稽胡千餘人，釋其酋帥數十人，授以官爵，使還，招其餘黨，劉屳成亦降。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Jiancheng captured more than a thousand Ji-Hu; he released several dozen of their chieftains, granted them offices and titles, and sent them back to win over the rest of their followers; Liu Wancheng also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Li Jiancheng took more than a thousand Ji-Hu captives. He freed several dozen of their chiefs, gave them offices and titles, and sent them back to rally the rest of the band; Liu Wancheng surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 建成詐稱增置州縣，築城邑，命降胡年二十以上皆集，以兵圍而殺之，死者六千餘人。

translations.literal: Jiancheng falsely announced that new prefectures and counties would be established and walled towns built, and ordered all surrendered Hu aged twenty or above to assemble; then he surrounded them with troops and killed them—more than six thousand dead.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng pretended that new prefectures and counties would be created and walled towns built, and ordered every surrendered Hu aged twenty or older to gather. He then surrounded them with troops and slaughtered them; more than six thousand died.

sentences.zh: 屳成覺變，亡奔梁師都。

translations.literal: Wancheng perceived the treachery and fled to Liang Shidu.
translations.idiomatic: Wancheng sensed the trap and fled to Liang Shidu.

sentences.zh: 行軍總管劉世讓攻竇建德黃州，拔之。

translations.literal: Campaign commander Liu Shirang attacked Dou Jiande's Huangzhou and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign commander Liu Shirang attacked Huangzhou, held by Dou Jiande, and captured it.

sentences.zh: 洺州嚴備，世讓不得進。

translations.literal: Mingzhou was on strict guard, and Shirang could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhou stood on full alert, and Shirang could not push forward.

sentences.zh: 會突厥將入寇，上召世讓還。

translations.literal: Just then the Turks were about to invade, and the emperor recalled Shirang.
translations.idiomatic: As the Turks were about to raid, the emperor recalled Shirang.

sentences.zh: 竇建德所署普樂令平恩程名振來降，上遙除名振永寧令，使將兵徇河北。

translations.literal: Cheng Mingzhen of Ping'en, whom Dou Jiande had appointed magistrate of Pule, came over in surrender; the emperor remotely appointed Mingzhen magistrate of Yongning and ordered him to lead troops to subdue Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Mingzhen of Ping'en—whom Dou Jiande had made magistrate of Pule—surrendered. The emperor appointed him magistrate of Yongning at a distance and sent him to lead troops through Hebei.

sentences.zh: 名振夜襲鄴，俘其男女千餘人。

translations.literal: Mingzhen raided Ye by night and took more than a thousand men and women captive.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhen struck Ye by night and seized more than a thousand men and women.

sentences.zh: 去鄴八十里，閱婦人乳有湩者九十餘人，悉縱遣之。

translations.literal: Eighty li from Ye, he examined women whose milk showed curdling and found more than ninety; he released them all.
translations.idiomatic: Eighty li from Ye, he found more than ninety women whose milk showed curdling—a sign they were still nursing infants—and set them all free.

sentences.zh: 鄴人感其仁，為之飯僧。

translations.literal: The people of Ye were moved by his benevolence and fed monks on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Ye, touched by his mercy, offered meals to monks in his honor.

sentences.zh: 突厥頡利可汗承父兄之資，士馬雄盛，有憑陵中國之志。

translations.literal: The Turkic qaghan Jieli, inheriting the resources of his father and elder brothers, had strong soldiers and horses and harbored the ambition to dominate China.
translations.idiomatic: The Turkic qaghan Jieli had inherited his father and brothers' strength; his warriors and horses were formidable, and he meant to dominate China.

sentences.zh: 妻隋義成公主，公主從弟善經，避亂在突厥，與王世充使者王文素共說頡利曰：「昔啟民為兄弟所逼，脫身奔隋。

translations.literal: He had married the Sui Princess Yicheng; the princess's cousin Shanjing, who had fled the turmoil and was living among the Turks, together with Wang Shichong's envoy Wang Wensu, urged Jieli, saying: "In the past Qimin was pressed by his brothers and fled to the Sui for refuge.
translations.idiomatic: He had married the Sui Princess Yicheng. Her cousin Shanjing, who had taken refuge with the Turks during the chaos, joined Wang Shichong's envoy Wang Wensu in urging Jieli: "Long ago Qimin was driven out by his brothers and fled to the Sui.

sentences.zh: 賴文皇帝之力，有此土宇，子孫享之。

translations.literal: Relying on Emperor Wen's power, he gained this territory, and his descendants enjoy it.
translations.idiomatic: With Emperor Wen's help he won this realm, and his descendants still hold it.

sentences.zh: 今唐天子非文皇帝子孫，可汗宜奉楊政道以伐之，以報文皇帝之德。

translations.literal: Now the Tang Son of Heaven is not a descendant of Emperor Wen; the qaghan ought to install Yang Zhengdao and attack them, to repay Emperor Wen's kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Today's Tang emperor is no descendant of Emperor Wen. You should set up Yang Zhengdao and march against Tang—to repay Emperor Wen's kindness.

sentences.zh: 」頡利然之。

translations.literal: " Jieli agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Jieli was persuaded.

sentences.zh: 上以中國未寧，待突厥甚厚，而頡利求請無厭，言辭驕慢。

translations.literal: Because China was not yet at peace, the emperor treated the Turks very generously, but Jieli's demands were insatiable and his words arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: With China still unsettled, the emperor treated the Turks with great generosity, yet Jieli's demands never ceased and his tone grew haughty.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，突厥寇汾陰。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, the Turks raided Fenyin.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiaxu, the Turks raided Fenyin.

sentences.zh: 唐兵圍洛陽，掘塹築壘而守之。

translations.literal: Tang troops besieged Luoyang, digging moats and building ramparts to hold the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Tang forces besieged Luoyang, digging trenches and building ramparts to hold the lines.

sentences.zh: 城中乏食，絹一匹直粟三升，布一匹直鹽一升，服飾珍玩，賤如土芥。

translations.literal: Food in the city ran short; one bolt of silk traded for three sheng of grain, one bolt of cloth for one sheng of salt; clothing and precious curios were cheap as weeds.
translations.idiomatic: Food inside the city ran out. A bolt of silk bought three sheng of grain; a bolt of cloth bought one sheng of salt. Finery and jewels were worthless as weeds.

sentences.zh: 民食草根木葉皆盡，相與澄取浮泥，投米屑作餅食之，皆病，身腫腳弱，死者相枕倚於道。

translations.literal: The people had eaten every root and leaf; they together strained floating mud, mixed in rice bran to make cakes and ate them—all fell ill, bodies swollen and legs weak; the dead lay piled along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: The people had eaten every root and leaf. They strained mud from ponds, mixed in rice bran to bake cakes, and ate them—all fell sick, swollen and weak; corpses lined the roads.

sentences.zh: 皇泰主之遷民入宮城也，凡三萬家，至是無三千家。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huangtai had moved the people into the palace city, there had been thirty thousand households in all; by now fewer than three thousand remained.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huangtai had moved the populace into the palace quarter, there had been thirty thousand households; now fewer than three thousand remained.

sentences.zh: 雖貴為公卿，糠核不充，尚書郎以下，親自負戴，往往餒死。

translations.literal: Even those noble as grand ministers could not fill themselves with chaff and husks; officials below the rank of Secretariat gentleman carried loads on their own backs and often starved to death.
translations.idiomatic: Even grand ministers could not fill their bellies with chaff. Secretariat gentlemen and lower ranks carried supplies on their own backs, and many starved.

sentences.zh: 竇建德使其將范願守曹州，悉發孟海公、徐圓朗之眾，西救洛陽。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande had his general Fan Yuan defend Caozhou, mustered all the forces of Meng Haigong and Xu Yuanlang, and marched west to relieve Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande left his general Fan Yuan to hold Caozhou, called up every soldier of Meng Haigong and Xu Yuanlang, and marched west to save Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 至滑州，王世充行臺僕射韓洪開門納之。

translations.literal: When they reached Huazhou, Wang Shichong's mobile headquarters vice director Han Hong opened the gates and admitted them.
translations.idiomatic: At Huazhou, Wang Shichong's mobile headquarters vice director Han Hong opened the gates and let them in.

sentences.zh: 己卯，軍於酸棗。

translations.literal: On jimao, the army encamped at Suanzao.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jimao, the army encamped at Suanzao.

sentences.zh: 壬午，突厥寇石州，刺史王集擊卻之。

translations.literal: On renwu, the Turks raided Shizhou; prefect Wang Ji drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renwu, the Turks raided Shizhou; Prefect Wang Ji repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 竇建德陷管州，殺刺史郭士安；

translations.literal: Dou Jiande took Guanzhou and killed prefect Guo Shi'an;
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande captured Guanzhou and killed Prefect Guo Shi'an;

sentences.zh: 又陷滎陽、陽翟等縣，水陸並進，泛舟運糧，溯河西上。

translations.literal: He also took Xingyang, Yangdi, and other counties, advancing by land and water alike, floating boats to transport grain and moving upriver along the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: He also seized Xingyang, Yangdi, and other counties, advancing by land and water, shipping grain by boat up the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 王世充之弟徐州行臺世辯遣其將郭士衡，將兵數千會之，合十餘萬，號三十萬，軍於成皋之東原，築宮板渚，遣使與王世充相聞。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong's younger brother Shibian of the Xuzhou mobile headquarters sent his general Guo Shiheng with several thousand troops to join him; together they mustered more than a hundred thousand and claimed three hundred thousand, encamping on the eastern plain of Chenggao, building a palace at Banzhu, and sending envoys to communicate with Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong's brother Shibian, head of the Xuzhou mobile headquarters, sent General Guo Shiheng with several thousand men to join him. Their combined host exceeded a hundred thousand; they claimed three hundred thousand, camped on the eastern plain of Chenggao, built a palace at Banzhu, and exchanged messages with Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 先是，建德遺秦王世民書，請退軍潼關，返鄭侵地，復修前好。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jiande had sent a letter to Prince of Qin Shimin, asking him to withdraw his army to Tong Pass, return the Zheng territories he had seized, and restore their former friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jiande had written to the Prince of Qin, Li Shimin, asking him to pull back to Tong Pass, return Zheng's seized lands, and renew their old friendship.

sentences.zh: 世民集將佐議之，皆請避其鋒，郭孝恪曰：「世充窮蹙，垂將面縛，建德遠來助之，此天意欲兩亡之也。

translations.literal: Shimin gathered his generals and staff to discuss it; all urged avoiding their edge. Guo Xiaoke said: "Shichong is at his wit's end and about to be bound with his face covered; Jiande has come from afar to aid him—this is Heaven's intent to destroy them both.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin called his officers to council; all urged giving way before the enemy's momentum. Guo Xiaoke said: "Shichong is cornered and about to surrender in bonds; Jiande has marched far to rescue him. Heaven means to destroy them both.

sentences.zh: 宜據武牢之險以拒之，伺間而動，破之必矣。

translations.literal: We ought to hold the defiles of Wulao to block him, watch for an opening to strike, and defeat him is certain."
translations.idiomatic: Hold the passes at Wulao, strike when the moment comes, and he will surely be broken."

sentences.zh: 」記室薛收曰：「世充保據東都，府庫充實，所將之兵，皆江、淮精銳，即日之患，但乏糧食耳。

translations.literal: Secretary Xue Shou said: "Shichong holds the Eastern Capital, his treasuries are full, and the troops he leads are all elite from the Yangzi and Huai—his present trouble is only lack of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Secretary Xue Shou said: "Shichong holds the Eastern Capital with full storehouses and Yangzi-Huai elite troops. His only trouble now is hunger.

sentences.zh: 以是之故，為我所持，求戰不得，守則難久。

translations.literal: For this reason we have him in our grip: he cannot get the battle he seeks, and if he holds out he cannot last long.
translations.idiomatic: That is why we have him pinned—he cannot force a battle, and he cannot endure a siege.

sentences.zh: 建德親帥大眾，遠來赴援，亦當極其精銳，致死於我。

translations.literal: Jiande personally leads a great host from afar to the rescue; he too will bring his finest troops and fight us to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande is coming in person with a great army from afar; he too will bring his best and fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 若縱之至此，兩寇合從，轉河北之粟以饋洛陽，則戰爭方始，偃兵無日，混一之期，殊未有涯也。

translations.literal: If we let him reach here, the two foes will join forces and shift Hebei's grain to feed Luoyang—then war has only begun, peace will have no day, and the time of unification is far beyond reach.
translations.idiomatic: If we let him arrive, the two enemies will unite and pipe Hebei's grain into Luoyang. War will only have begun; peace will be distant; unification will be nowhere in sight.

sentences.zh: 今宜分兵守洛陽，深溝高壘，世充出兵，慎勿與戰，大王親帥驍銳，先據成皋，厲兵訓士，以待其至，以逸待勞，決可克也。

translations.literal: Now we should divide troops to hold Luoyang with deep moats and high ramparts; if Shichong sallies, take care not to fight; Your Highness should personally lead the crack troops, seize Chenggao first, sharpen weapons and train the men, and await his arrival—fresh against weary, victory is assured."
translations.idiomatic: Split your forces to hold Luoyang behind deep trenches and high walls; if Shichong sallies, do not engage. Your Highness should lead the elite to Chenggao first, drill your men, and wait for Jiande—fresh against weary, you will surely win."

sentences.zh: 建德既破，世充自下，不過二旬，兩主就縛矣。

translations.literal: Once Jiande is broken, Shichong will fall of himself—in no more than twenty days both lords will be bound."
translations.idiomatic: Break Jiande, and Shichong will collapse on his own. Within twenty days both rulers will be in bonds.

sentences.zh: 」世民善之。

translations.literal: Shimin approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 收，道衡之子也。

translations.literal: Shou was the son of Xue Daoheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was a son of Xue Daoheng.

sentences.zh: 蕭瑀、屈突通、封德彝皆曰：「吾兵疲老，世充憑守堅城，未易猝拔，建德席勝而來，鋒銳氣盛；

translations.literal: Xiao Yu, Qu Tu Tong, and Feng Deyi all said: "Our troops are weary and aged; Shichong relies on a strong walled city and cannot be taken in a rush; Jiande comes riding on victory, his edge sharp and his spirit high;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu, Qu Tu Tong, and Feng Deyi all argued: "Our men are worn and old. Shichong holds a strong city and cannot be stormed quickly. Jiande comes fresh from victory, keen and bold;

sentences.zh: 吾腹背受敵，非完策也，不若退保新安，以承其弊。

translations.literal: we are struck front and rear—this is no perfect plan; better to withdraw and hold Xin'an, waiting to profit from their exhaustion."
translations.idiomatic: we would be caught between two foes. That is no safe plan. Better fall back on Xin'an and wait for them to wear themselves out."

sentences.zh: 」世民曰：「世充兵摧食盡，上下離心，不煩力攻，可以坐克。

translations.literal: Shimin said: "Shichong's troops are broken and his food gone; above and below are divided in heart—no need for strenuous attack; he can be taken sitting down.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin said: "Shichong's army is shattered and his granaries empty; his court and camp are divided. We need not fight hard—we can take him without stirring.

sentences.zh: 建德新破海公，將驕卒惰，吾據武牢，扼其咽喉。

translations.literal: Jiande has newly defeated Haigong; his generals are arrogant and his soldiers slack. We hold Wulao and choke his throat.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande has just beaten Haigong; his officers are proud and his men lax. We hold Wulao and grip his throat.

sentences.zh: 彼若冒險爭鋒，吾取之甚易。

translations.literal: If they rashly contest the field, we take them very easily.
translations.idiomatic: If they dare to fight, we will beat them with ease.

sentences.zh: 若狐疑不戰，旬月之間，世充自潰。

translations.literal: If they hesitate and do not fight, within a month or so Shichong will collapse of himself.
translations.idiomatic: If they hesitate and hold back, Shichong will fall apart within a month.

sentences.zh: 城破兵強，氣勢自倍，一舉兩克，在此行矣。

translations.literal: When the city falls our troops will be strong and our momentum will double—two victories in one stroke lies in this march.
translations.idiomatic: When the city falls our strength will double. Two victories in one campaign—that is what this march will bring.

sentences.zh: 若不速進，賊入武牢，諸城新附，必不能守；

translations.literal: If we do not advance quickly and the enemy enters Wulao, the cities newly submitted will surely not be held;
translations.idiomatic: If we delay and the enemy seizes Wulao, every city that has just submitted will be lost;

sentences.zh: 兩賊並力，其勢必強，何弊之承？

translations.literal: the two foes united—their power will surely be strong—what exhaustion shall we inherit?"
translations.idiomatic: united, the two foes will only grow stronger. What exhaustion will we inherit then?"

sentences.zh: 吾計決矣！

translations.literal: My plan is settled!"
translations.idiomatic: My mind is made up!"

sentences.zh: 」通等又請解圍據險以觀其變，世民不許。

translations.literal: Tong and the others again asked to lift the siege and hold the defiles to watch how matters changed; Shimin would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Tong and the others again urged lifting the siege and holding the passes to see how events unfolded. Shimin refused.

sentences.zh: 中分麾下，使通等副齊王元吉圍守東都，世民將驍勇三千五百人東趣武牢。

translations.literal: He divided his command in half, leaving Tong and the others to assist Prince of Qi Yuanji in besieging the Eastern Capital, while Shimin led three thousand five hundred crack troops east toward Wulao.
translations.idiomatic: He split his army: Tong and the rest would assist Prince of Qi Li Yuanji in besieging the Eastern Capital, while Shimin led thirty-five hundred elite troops east to Wulao.

sentences.zh: 時正晝出兵，歷北邙，抵河陽，趨鞏而去。

translations.literal: It was broad daylight when he marched out; he passed along the Northern Mang, reached Heyang, and hurried on toward Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He marched out in broad daylight, crossed the Northern Mang hills, reached Heyang, and pressed on toward Gong.

sentences.zh: 王世充登城望見，莫之測也，竟不敢出。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong mounted the wall and watched; he could not fathom it and in the end dared not sally.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong watched from the walls, unable to guess his intent, and never dared to sally.

sentences.zh: 癸未，世民入武牢；

translations.literal: On guiwei, Shimin entered Wulao;
translations.idiomatic: On the day guiwei, Shimin entered Wulao;

sentences.zh: 甲申，將驍騎五百，出武牢東二十餘里，覘建德之營。

translations.literal: on jiashen he led five hundred crack horsemen more than twenty li east of Wulao to reconnoiter Jiande's camp.
translations.idiomatic: on jiashen he took five hundred crack horsemen more than twenty li east of Wulao to scout Jiande's camp.

sentences.zh: 緣道分留從騎，使李世勣、程知節、秦叔寶分將之，伏於道旁，才餘四騎，與之偕進。

translations.literal: Along the road he left detachments of his escort, having Li Shiji, Cheng Zhijie, and Qin Shubao each command part of them in ambush by the roadside; only four horsemen remained to advance with him.
translations.idiomatic: Along the road he posted escorts in ambush under Li Shiji, Cheng Zhijie, and Qin Shubao, then rode on with only four companions.

sentences.zh: 世民謂尉遲敬德曰：「吾執弓矢，公執槊相隨，雖百萬眾若我何！

translations.literal: Shimin said to Yuchi Jingde: "I shall hold bow and arrow, you shall hold the spear and follow—what can a million men do to us!"
translations.idiomatic: Shimin told Yuchi Jingde: "I will take the bow; you take the spear. Even a million men cannot touch us!"

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「賊見我而還，上策也。

translations.literal: He added: "If the enemy sees me and withdraws, that is the best plan."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Best if they see us and turn back."

sentences.zh: 」去建德營三里所，建德遊兵遇之，以為斥候也。

translations.literal: About three li from Jiande's camp, Jiande's patrol troops met them and took them for scouts.
translations.idiomatic: Three li from Jiande's camp, patrols met them and took them for scouts.

sentences.zh: 世民大呼曰：「我秦王也。

translations.literal: Shimin shouted: "I am the Prince of Qin."
translations.idiomatic: Shimin shouted: "I am the Prince of Qin."

sentences.zh: 」引弓射之，斃其一將。

translations.literal: He drew his bow and shot, killing one of their officers.
translations.idiomatic: He loosed an arrow and killed one of their officers.

sentences.zh: 建德軍中大驚，出五六千騎逐之；

translations.literal: Jiande's army was greatly alarmed and sent out five or six thousand horsemen in pursuit;
translations.idiomatic: Jiande's camp was thrown into alarm; five or six thousand horsemen galloped after them;

sentences.zh: 從者咸失色，世民曰：「汝弟前行，吾自與敬德為殿。

translations.literal: his companions all turned pale; Shimin said: "You younger brothers go ahead; I and Jingde will bring up the rear ourselves."
translations.idiomatic: his companions paled. Shimin said: "You go on ahead; Jingde and I will cover the rear."

sentences.zh: 」於是按轡徐行，追騎將至，則引弓射之，輒斃一人。

translations.literal: Then he reined in and walked his horse slowly; whenever the pursuers were about to reach him, he drew his bow and shot, and each time killed a man.
translations.idiomatic: He slowed his horse. Whenever pursuers drew near, he shot—and each arrow dropped a man.

sentences.zh: 追者懼而止，止而復來，如是再三，每來必有斃者，世民前後射殺數人，敬德殺十許人，追者不敢復逼。

translations.literal: The pursuers feared and halted; halting, they came again—so three and four times; each time they came there were dead; Shimin shot and killed several in all, Jingde killed about ten, and the pursuers dared press no further.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuers halted in fear, then came on again—again and again. Each charge cost them lives. Shimin killed several with his bow; Jingde killed about ten. At last they dared not close in.

sentences.zh: 世民逡巡稍卻以誘之，入於伏內，世勣等奮擊，大破之，斬首三百餘級，獲其驍將殷秋、石瓚以歸。

translations.literal: Shimin lingered and drew back slightly to lure them, leading them into the ambush; Li Shiji and the others struck fiercely and routed them utterly, taking more than three hundred heads and capturing their fierce generals Yin Qiu and Shi Zan in return.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin feigned retreat and drew them into the ambush. Li Shiji and the others charged and routed them, taking more than three hundred heads and capturing the fierce generals Yin Qiu and Shi Zan.

sentences.zh: 乃為書報建德，諭以「趙魏之地，久為我有，為足下所侵奪。

translations.literal: He then wrote to inform Jiande, explaining: "The lands of Zhao and Wei have long been ours, yet were seized by you.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote to Jiande: "The lands of Zhao and Wei have long been ours, yet you seized them.

sentences.zh: 但以淮安見禮，公主得歸，故相與坦懷釋怨。

translations.literal: Only because Huai'an was treated with courtesy and the princess was allowed to return did we open our hearts and release our grievances.
translations.idiomatic: Because Huai'an was honored and the princess sent home, we laid our grievances aside.

sentences.zh: 世充頃與足下修好，已嘗反覆，今亡在朝夕，更飾辭相誘，足下乃以三軍之眾，仰哺他人，千金之資，坐供外費，良非上策。

translations.literal: Shichong not long ago made peace with you, yet has already turned again; now his fall is within morning and evening, yet he still decks his words to entice you—you use the host of three armies to feed at another's table and sit on a fortune of a thousand gold to supply an outsider's costs; this is truly no superior plan.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong made peace with you not long ago and has already betrayed you. He is doomed within days, yet he still flatters you into war. You feed your whole army at another man's table and spend your treasure on a stranger—that is no wise course.

sentences.zh: 今前茅相遇，彼遽崩摧，郊勞未通，能無懷愧！

translations.literal: Now our vanguards have met and they have suddenly collapsed—before the suburban greeting could be exchanged, can you not feel shame!
translations.idiomatic: Our vanguards have already met, and his front ranks have crumbled. You have not even been welcomed in the suburbs—should you not feel ashamed!

sentences.zh: 故抑止鋒銳，冀聞擇善；

translations.literal: Therefore I have restrained my sharp edge, hoping you will hear and choose what is good;
translations.idiomatic: I have held back my army, hoping you will choose wisely;

sentences.zh: 若不獲命，恐雖悔難追。

translations.literal: if I do not receive your assent, I fear that though you regret, it will be hard to pursue."
translations.idiomatic: if you refuse, regret may come too late to undo."

sentences.zh: 立秦王世民之子泰為衛王。

translations.literal: Shimin's son Tai was established as Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin's son Li Tai was made Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己丑，豐州總管張長遜入朝。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jichou, Fengzhou regional commander Zhang Changsun came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the day jichou, Fengzhou regional commander Zhang Changsun came to court.

sentences.zh: 時言事者多雲，長遜久居豐州，為突厥所厚，非國家之利。

translations.literal: At the time many who spoke on affairs said that Changsun had long resided at Fengzhou and was favored by the Turks—this was not to the state's benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Many at court said Changsun's long tenure at Fengzhou had won him favor with the Turks, to the state's harm.

sentences.zh: 長遜聞之，請入朝，上許之。

translations.literal: Changsun heard of this and asked to come to court; the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Changsun asked to come to court, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 會太子建成北伐稽胡，長遜帥所部會之，因入朝，拜右武候將軍。

translations.literal: It happened that Crown Prince Jiancheng was campaigning north against the Ji-Hu; Changsun led his command to join him, then entered court and was appointed General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Li Jiancheng was campaigning north against the Ji-Hu; Changsun brought his troops to join him, then came to court and was made General of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 益州行臺左僕射竇軌帥巴、蜀兵來會秦王擊王世充，以長遜檢校益州行臺右僕射。

translations.literal: Dou Gui, left vice director of the Yizhou mobile headquarters, was leading Ba and Shu troops to join the Prince of Qin against Wang Shichong; Changsun was made acting right vice director of the Yizhou mobile headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Gui, left vice director of the Yizhou mobile headquarters, was leading Ba and Shu troops to join the Prince of Qin against Wang Shichong; Changsun was appointed acting right vice director of the same headquarters.

sentences.zh: 己亥，突厥頡利可汗寇雁門，李大恩擊走之。

translations.literal: On jihai, the Turkic qaghan Jieli raided Yanmen; Li Da'en drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jihai, the Turkic qaghan Jieli raided Yanmen; Li Da'en repulsed him.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，王世充騎將楊公卿、單雄信引兵出戰，齊王元吉擊之，不利，行軍總管盧君諤戰死。

translations.literal: On renyin, Wang Shichong's cavalry generals Yang Gongqing and Shan Xiongxin led troops out to fight; Prince of Qi Yuanji attacked them but fared ill, and campaign commander Lu Jun'e died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renyin, Wang Shichong's cavalry generals Yang Gongqing and Shan Xiongxin sallied. Prince of Qi Li Yuanji attacked but fared badly; campaign commander Lu Jun'e was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 太子還長安。

translations.literal: The crown prince returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 王世充平州刺史周仲隱以城來降。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhongyin, Wang Shichong's prefect of Pingzhou, surrendered his city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhongyin, Wang Shichong's prefect of Pingzhou, surrendered his city.

sentences.zh: 戊申，突厥寇并州。

translations.literal: On wushen, the Turks raided Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wushen, the Turks raided Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，處羅可汗與劉武周相表裡，寇并州；

translations.literal: Earlier, Qaghan Chuluo had acted in concert with Liu Wuzhou to raid Bingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Qaghan Chuluo had joined Liu Wuzhou in raiding Bingzhou;

sentences.zh: 上遣太常卿鄭元□往諭以禍福，處羅不從。

translations.literal: the emperor sent Director of Imperial Sacrifices Zheng Yuankui to instruct him on fortune and disaster, but Chuluo would not heed.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor sent Director of Imperial Sacrifices Zheng Yuankui to warn him of the consequences, but Chuluo refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 未幾，處羅遇疾卒，國人疑元□毒之，留不遣。

translations.literal: Before long Chuluo fell ill and died; his people suspected Yuankui had poisoned him and detained him without release.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chuluo fell ill and died. His people suspected Yuankui of poisoning him and held him captive.

sentences.zh: 上又遣漢陽公瓖賂頡利可汗以金帛，頡利慾令瑰拜，瑰不從，亦留之。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent Duke of Hanyang Gui with gold and silks to bribe Qaghan Jieli; Jieli wished to make Gui perform obeisance, but Gui would not comply and was also detained.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sent Duke of Hanyang Li Gui with gold and silks to bribe Qaghan Jieli. Jieli demanded that Gui bow to him; Gui refused and was detained as well.

sentences.zh: 又留左驍衛大將軍長孫順德。

translations.literal: They also detained Left Martial Guard General Zhangsun Shunde.
translations.idiomatic: They also detained Left Martial Guard General Zhangsun Shunde.

sentences.zh: 上怒，亦留其使者。

translations.literal: The emperor in anger likewise detained their envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, angered, detained their envoys in turn.

sentences.zh: 瑰，孝恭之弟也。

translations.literal: Gui was the younger brother of Xiaogong.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was a younger brother of Li Xiaogong.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，封皇子元方為周王，元禮為鄭王，元嘉為宋王，元則為荊王，元茂為越王。

translations.literal: On jiayin, the princes Yuanfang was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhou, Yuanli as Prince of Zheng, Yuanjia as Prince of Song, Yuanze as Prince of Jing, and Yuanmao as Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiayin, Prince Yuanfang was made Prince of Zhou, Yuanli Prince of Zheng, Yuanjia Prince of Song, Yuanze Prince of Jing, and Yuanmao Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 竇建德迫於武牢不得進，留屯累月，戰數不利，將士思歸。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande, pressed at Wulao and unable to advance, remained encamped for months; battles went ill several times, and officers and soldiers longed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Blocked at Wulao, Dou Jiande could not advance. He camped there for months, lost several fights, and his men yearned for home.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，秦王世民遣王君廓將輕騎千餘抄其糧運，又破之，獲其大將軍張青特。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Prince of Qin Shimin sent Wang Junkuo with more than a thousand light horsemen to raid his grain convoys; he broke them again and captured his great general Zhang Qingte.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingsi, the Prince of Qin sent Wang Junkuo with more than a thousand light cavalry to raid Jiande's grain trains. He routed them again and captured the great general Zhang Qingte.

sentences.zh: 凌敬言於建德曰：「大王悉兵濟河，攻取懷州、河陽，使重將守之，更鳴鼓建旗，逾太行，入上黨，徇汾、晉，趣蒲津，如此有三利：一則蹈無人之境，取勝可以萬全；

translations.literal: Ling Jing said to Jiande: "Great King, lead all your troops across the river, take Huaizhou and Heyang, leave heavy generals to hold them, then beat drums and raise banners again, cross the Taihang, enter Shangdang, subdue Fen and Jin, and hasten to Pujin—in this way there are three benefits: first, you tread an unpeopled land and victory can be wholly secure;
translations.idiomatic: Ling Jing urged Jiande: "My lord, take your whole army across the river, seize Huaizhou and Heyang, and leave trusted generals to hold them. Then beat the drums, raise your banners, cross the Taihang, enter Shangdang, sweep Fen and Jin, and strike for Pujin. That course offers three gains: first, you march through empty country and can win without risk;

sentences.zh: 二則拓地收眾，形勢益強；

translations.literal: second, you expand territory and gather followers, and your position grows stronger;
translations.idiomatic: second, you widen your lands and swell your ranks, and your power grows;

sentences.zh: 三則關中震駭，鄭圍自解。

translations.literal: Third, Guanzhong would be shaken with terror, and the siege of Zheng would resolve itself.
translations.idiomatic: Third, it would terrify Guanzhong, and the siege of Luoyang would lift of its own accord.

sentences.zh: 為今之策，無以易此。

translations.literal: As a policy for the present, nothing can replace this.
translations.idiomatic: For the present situation, there is no better course than this.

sentences.zh: 」建德將從之，而王世充遣使告急相繼於道，王琬、長孫安世朝夕涕泣，請救洛陽，又陰以金玉啖建德諸將，以撓其謀。

translations.literal: Jiande was about to follow this, but Wang Shichong sent envoys in unbroken succession on the road with urgent appeals; Wang Wan and Zhangsun Anshi wept day and night, pleading for relief for Luoyang, and also secretly used gold and jade to win over Jiande's generals, to undermine his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande was on the point of accepting this counsel, but Wang Shichong's messengers came one after another with cries for help; Wang Wan and Zhangsun Anshi wept day and night, begging him to save Luoyang, while secretly bribing Jiande's generals with gold and jade to thwart his strategy.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆曰：「凌敬書生，安知戰事，其言豈可用也！

translations.literal: The generals all said: "Ling Jing is a mere scholar—how could he know anything of warfare? How could his words be used!"
translations.idiomatic: The generals all said, "Ling Jing is a bookish man—what does he know of battle? His advice is worthless!"

sentences.zh: 」建德乃謝敬曰：「今眾心甚銳，天讚我也，因之決戰，必將大捷，不得從公言。

translations.literal: Jiande then apologized to Jing, saying: "Now the men's hearts are very keen—Heaven approves of me. Seizing this moment for a decisive battle, we are sure to win a great victory. I cannot follow your counsel."
translations.idiomatic: Jiande then declined Ling Jing's advice: "Our troops' spirits are high and Heaven favors us. If we fight a decisive battle now, victory is certain. I cannot take your counsel."

sentences.zh: 」敬固爭之，建德怒，令扶出。

translations.literal: Jing pressed his argument firmly; Jiande grew angry and ordered him carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Jing argued all the more fiercely; Jiande flew into a rage and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 其妻曹氏謂建德曰：「祭酒之言不可違也。

translations.literal: His wife, Lady Cao, said to Jiande: "The Intendant's words must not be disobeyed."
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Cao said to him, "You must not disregard the Intendant's counsel."

sentences.zh: 今大王自滏口乘唐國之虛，連營漸進，以取山北，又因突厥西抄關中，唐必還師自救，鄭圍何憂不解！

translations.literal: Now if Your Majesty advances from Fankou while the Tang state is weakened, encamping in succession and pressing forward to take the area north of the mountains, and moreover relies on the Turks to raid Guanzhong from the west, the Tang are sure to withdraw their army to save themselves—why worry that the siege of Zheng will not be lifted!
translations.idiomatic: If you now march from Fankou while the Tang is overextended, advance in successive camps to seize the lands north of the mountains, and have the Turks strike Guanzhong from the west, the Tang will surely recall their armies to defend themselves—and the siege of Luoyang will lift without a fight!

sentences.zh: 若頓兵於此，老師費財，欲求成功，在於何日？

translations.literal: If you halt your army here, the troops grow stale and expenses mount—on what day do you expect success?
translations.idiomatic: If you halt the army here, your soldiers will weary and your treasury drain—when do you expect to succeed?

sentences.zh: 」建德曰：「此非女子所知！

translations.literal: Jiande said: "This is not something a woman would understand!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiande replied, "This is beyond a woman's understanding!"

sentences.zh: 吾來救鄭，鄭今倒懸，亡在朝夕，吾乃捨之而去，是畏敵而棄信也，不可。

translations.literal: I came to rescue Zheng; Zheng now hangs by a thread, destruction imminent within days—if I abandon them and leave, that would be to fear the enemy and break faith. It cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: I came to rescue Zheng; Zheng now hangs by a thread and will perish within days. To abandon them and withdraw would be to show fear of the enemy and betray my promise—that I cannot do.

sentences.zh: 諜者告曰：「建德伺唐軍芻盡，牧馬於河北，將襲武牢。

translations.literal: A spy reported: "Jiande, watching until the Tang army's fodder was exhausted, is pasturing horses north of the river and intends to strike Wulao."
translations.idiomatic: Spies reported, "Jiande, waiting until the Tang ran out of fodder, is grazing horses north of the river and plans to attack Wulao."

sentences.zh: 」五月，戊午，秦王世民北濟河，南臨廣武，察敵形勢，因留馬千餘匹，牧於河渚以誘之，夕還武牢。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day wuwu, Prince of Qin Shimin crossed the river to the north, then pressed south to Guangwu to observe the enemy's disposition; he left more than a thousand horses grazing on the river islets to lure them, and at evening returned to Wulao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day wuwu, the Prince of Qin Shimin crossed the Yellow River to the north, then moved south to Guangwu to reconnoiter the enemy. He left over a thousand horses grazing on the river flats as bait, then returned to Wulao at dusk.

sentences.zh: 己未，建德果悉眾而至，自板渚出牛口置陳，北距大河，西薄汜水，南屬鵲山，亙二十里，鼓行而進。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei, Jiande did indeed bring his entire force; deploying his battle line from Banshu through Niukou, with the great river to the north, pressing close to Sishui on the west, linked to Que Mountain on the south, spanning twenty li, they advanced with drums beating.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Jiande arrived in full force, deploying his line from Banshu through Niukou—with the great river to the north, Sishui to the west, and Que Mountain to the south—stretching twenty li, they advanced to the beat of drums.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆懼，世民將數騎升高丘以望之，謂諸將曰：「賊起山東，未嘗見大敵，今度險而囂，是無紀律，逼城而陳，有輕我心；

translations.literal: The generals were all afraid. Shimin took a few horsemen up a high mound to observe them and said to the generals: "These bandits rose in Shandong and have never faced a great enemy. Now they cross difficult terrain shouting loudly—they lack discipline. Drawing up battle lines close to the city shows they hold us in contempt."
translations.idiomatic: The generals were all afraid. Shimin rode with a few men to a high hill to watch them and told his officers, "These rebels rose in the east and have never met a real foe. They shout as they come through difficult terrain—undisciplined. Drawing up lines so close to our walls shows they underestimate us."

sentences.zh: 我按甲不出，彼勇氣自衰，陳久卒饑，勢將自退，追而擊之，無不克者。

translations.literal: If we hold our armor and do not sally forth, their fighting spirit will drain away of itself; long in formation the soldiers grow hungry, and their momentum will turn to retreat. Pursue and strike them—not one we cannot overcome.
translations.idiomatic: If we hold our position and refuse battle, their zeal will fade; kept long in formation, their men will hunger and the army will begin to withdraw. Then we pursue and strike—none will stand against us.

sentences.zh: 與公等約，甫過日中，必破之矣！

translations.literal: I wager with you all: barely past midday, we shall surely break them!
translations.idiomatic: I promise you—shortly after noon, we will crush them!

sentences.zh: 」建德意輕唐軍，遣三百騎涉汜水，距唐營一里所止。

translations.literal: Jiande held the Tang army in contempt. He sent three hundred cavalry across Sishui and halted about one li from the Tang camp.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande underestimated the Tang force. He sent three hundred horsemen across the Sishui and halted about a li from the Tang camp.

sentences.zh: 遣使與世民相聞曰：「請選銳士數百與之劇。

translations.literal: He sent a messenger to communicate with Shimin, saying: "Please select several hundred elite troops to contest fiercely with them."
translations.idiomatic: He sent a messenger to Shimin: "Choose several hundred of your best men and let us fight it out."

sentences.zh: 」世民遣王君廓將長槊二百以應之，相與交戰，乍進乍退，兩無勝負，各引還。

translations.literal: Shimin sent Wang Junkuo leading two hundred men with long spears to respond; they engaged in battle, now advancing, now retreating; neither side prevailed, and each withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin sent Wang Junkuo with two hundred long-spearmen to meet them. They traded blows, advancing and falling back by turns, with neither side gaining the upper hand, then each withdrew.

sentences.zh: 王琬乘隋煬帝□馬，鎧仗甚鮮，迥出陳前以誇眾。

translations.literal: Wang Wan rode Emperor Yang of Sui's □ horse; his armor and weapons were very splendid, and he rode far out in front of the battle line to show off before the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wan rode Emperor Yang's □ horse, his armor and arms gleaming bright; he rode far ahead of the lines to dazzle the army.

sentences.zh: 世民曰：「彼所乘真良馬也！

translations.literal: Shimin said: "The horse he rides is truly a fine steed!"
translations.idiomatic: Shimin said, "That is a fine horse he rides!"

sentences.zh: 」尉遲敬德請往取之，世民止之曰：「豈可以一馬喪猛士？

translations.literal: Yuchi Jingde asked to go seize it; Shimin stopped him, saying: "How could one lose a fierce warrior for the sake of a horse?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jingde asked leave to capture it, but Shimin restrained him: "Would you risk a great warrior's life for a horse?"

sentences.zh: 」敬德不從，與高甑生、梁建方三騎直入其陳，擒琬，引其馬以歸，眾無敢當者。

translations.literal: Jingde did not obey; with Gao Zengsheng and Liang Jianfang, three riders plunged straight into their battle line, captured Wan, and led his horse back; none dared stand in their way.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde paid no heed. With Gao Zengsheng and Liang Jianfang, the three horsemen charged straight into the enemy line, seized Wan, and rode off with his horse—no one dared oppose them.

sentences.zh: 世民使召河北馬，待其至，乃出戰。

translations.literal: Shimin had the horses from north of the river summoned; waiting until they arrived, he then went out to battle.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin sent for the horses grazing north of the river and waited until they arrived before committing to battle.

sentences.zh: 建德列陳，自辰至午，士卒饑倦，皆坐列，又爭飲水，逡巡欲退。

translations.literal: Jiande drew up his battle line; from the hour chen to wu the soldiers grew hungry and weary—all sat in their ranks, then scrambled for water, and hesitated, wanting to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande held his men in formation from morning until noon. Hungry and exhausted, the soldiers sat down in their ranks, then fought over water; soon they began to waver and wanted to pull back.

sentences.zh: 世民命宇文士及將三百騎經建德陳西，馳而南上，戒之曰：「賊若不動，爾宜引歸，動則引兵東出。

translations.literal: Shimin ordered Yuwen Shiji to lead three hundred cavalry past the west of Jiande's battle line, galloping southward up the slope, admonishing him: "If the bandits do not move, you should lead your men back; if they move, lead your troops out to the east."
translations.idiomatic: Shimin ordered Yuwen Shiji to take three hundred horsemen west of Jiande's line and ride south up the slope, telling him, "If the enemy holds steady, withdraw—but if they stir, swing your men eastward."

sentences.zh: 」士及至陳前，陳果動，世民曰：「可擊矣！

translations.literal: When Shiji reached the front of the battle line, the line indeed stirred; Shimin said: "They can be struck!"
translations.idiomatic: When Shiji reached the enemy front, the line did stir. Shimin cried, "Now we can strike!"

sentences.zh: 」時河渚馬亦至，乃命出戰。

translations.literal: At that time the horses from the river islets also arrived; he then ordered them out to battle.
translations.idiomatic: By then the horses from the river flats had also arrived, and he gave the order to attack.

sentences.zh: 世民帥輕騎先進，大軍繼之，東涉汜水，直薄其陳。

translations.literal: Shimin led light cavalry in the advance, the main army following; crossing Sishui to the east, they pressed straight upon their battle line.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin led the light cavalry forward with the main army close behind, crossed the Sishui to the east, and drove straight into the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 建德群臣方朝謁，唐騎猝來，朝臣趨就建德，建德召騎兵使拒唐兵，騎兵阻朝臣不得過，建德揮朝臣令卻，進退之間，唐兵已至，建德窘迫，退依東陂。

translations.literal: Jiande's ministers were just attending court audience when Tang cavalry suddenly arrived; the court officials rushed toward Jiande. Jiande summoned cavalry to repel the Tang troops, but the cavalry blocked the court officials from passing. Jiande waved the court officials to withdraw; in the confusion of advance and retreat, Tang troops had already arrived. Jiande was pressed hard and withdrew to rely on the eastern slope.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande's ministers were still at morning audience when Tang horsemen suddenly appeared. The officials rushed to Jiande's side; he called for cavalry to block the Tang attack, but the horsemen jammed the officials' path. Jiande waved the courtiers back—in that moment of confusion the Tang were upon them. Hard pressed, Jiande fell back toward the eastern slope.

sentences.zh: 竇抗引兵擊之，戰小不利。

translations.literal: Dou Kang led troops to strike them; the battle went slightly against them.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Kang led a counterattack, but met a temporary setback.

sentences.zh: 世民帥騎赴之，所向皆靡。

translations.literal: Shimin led cavalry to their aid; wherever he went, all crumbled before him.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin rode to their rescue; wherever he turned, the enemy broke before him.

sentences.zh: 淮陽王道玄挺身陷陳，直出其後，復突陳而歸，再入再出，飛矢集其身如□胃毛，勇氣不衰，射人，皆應弦而僕。

translations.literal: Prince of Huaiyang Li Daixuan thrust himself into the battle line, broke straight through to their rear, then burst through the line again to return—entering and leaving again and again. Flying arrows clustered on his body like □ on armor bristles; his courage did not flag. He shot men, and all fell at the twang of his bowstring.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huaiyang Li Daixuan plunged into the enemy lines, cut through to their rear, then burst back through—again and again he rode in and out. Arrows bristled on his body like □ hair on a cuirass, yet his valor never faltered; every man he shot fell at the twang of his bow.

sentences.zh: 世民給以副馬，使從己。

translations.literal: Shimin supplied him with a spare horse and had him follow himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin gave him a remount and kept him at his side.

sentences.zh: 於是諸軍大戰，塵埃漲天。

translations.literal: Thereupon the various armies joined in great battle; dust rose to fill the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Then the armies clashed in full fury, and dust blotted out the sky.

sentences.zh: 世民帥史大柰、程知節、秦叔寶、宇文歆等卷旆而入，出其陳後，張唐旗幟，建德將士顧見之，大潰；

translations.literal: Shimin led Shi Dana, Cheng Zhijie, Qin Shubao, Yuwen Xin, and others, flags furled, charging in and emerging behind their battle line; they unfurled Tang banners and flags. Jiande's officers and soldiers, looking back and seeing this, fled in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin led Shi Dana, Cheng Zhijie, Qin Shubao, Yuwen Xin, and others in a sweeping charge through the enemy rear, then raised the Tang banners. When Jiande's soldiers looked back and saw them, they broke and fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 追奔三十里，斬首三千餘級。

translations.literal: Pursuing the fleeing enemy for thirty li, they cut off more than three thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued the fleeing army for thirty li and took more than three thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 建德中槊，竄匿於牛口渚。

translations.literal: Jiande was struck by a spear; he fled and hid at Niukou shoal.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande was wounded by a spear and fled to hide at Niukou shoal.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍白士讓、楊武威逐之，建德墜馬，士讓援槊欲刺之，建德曰：「勿殺我，我夏王也，能富貴汝。

translations.literal: Cavalry General Bai Shirang and Yang Wuwei pursued him. Jiande fell from his horse; Shirang raised his spear intending to stab him. Jiande said: "Do not kill me—I am the King of Xia; I can make you rich and honored."
translations.idiomatic: The cavalry generals Bai Shirang and Yang Wuwei pursued him. Jiande fell from his horse; Shirang leveled his spear to run him through, but Jiande cried, "Spare me—I am the King of Xia! I can make you rich and noble."

sentences.zh: 」武威下擒之，載以從馬，來見世民。

translations.literal: Wuwei dismounted and captured him, loaded him on a spare horse, and came to see Shimin.
translations.idiomatic: Wuwei dismounted and seized him, put him on a spare horse, and brought him before Shimin.

sentences.zh: 世民讓之曰：「我自討王世充，何預汝事，而來越境，犯我兵鋒！

translations.literal: Shimin reproached him, saying: "I myself am campaigning against Wang Shichong—what concern is it of yours that you came crossing my borders and ran against the edge of my blades!"
translations.idiomatic: Shimin rebuked him: "I came to subdue Wang Shichong—what business was it of yours to cross my borders and clash with my army?"

sentences.zh: 」建德曰：「今不自來，恐煩遠取。

translations.literal: Jiande said: "Had I not come of my own accord, I feared you would be troubled to fetch me from afar."
translations.idiomatic: Jiande replied, "If I had not come myself, I feared it would trouble you to fetch me from so far away."

sentences.zh: 」建德將士皆潰去，所俘獲五萬人，世民即日散遣之，使還鄉里。

translations.literal: Jiande's officers and soldiers all fled and scattered; those captured amounted to fifty thousand men. Shimin that same day released and sent them off, letting them return to their home villages.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande's army melted away. Of the fifty thousand taken prisoner, Shimin released them all that same day to return home.

sentences.zh: 封德彝入賀，世民笑曰：「不用公言，得有今日。

translations.literal: Feng Deyi entered to offer congratulations; Shimin laughed and said: "By not heeding your counsel, I have gained this day."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Deyi came to offer congratulations. Shimin smiled and said, "By ignoring your advice, I have won this day."

sentences.zh: 智者千慮，不免一失乎！

translations.literal: Even the wise, in a thousand deliberations, cannot avoid one lapse!
translations.idiomatic: Even the wisest man, pondering a thousand times, cannot avoid one mistake!

sentences.zh: 」德彝甚慚。

translations.literal: Deyi was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Deyi was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 建德妻曹氏與左僕射齊善行將數百騎遁歸洺州。

translations.literal: Jiande's wife Lady Cao and Left Vice Director Qi Shanxing led several hundred horsemen in flight back to Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande's wife Lady Cao and Left Vice Director Qi Shanxing fled with several hundred horsemen back to Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲子，世充偃師、鞏縣皆降。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, Wang Shichong's Yanshi and Gong counties both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Yanshi and Gong counties, held by Wang Shichong, both surrendered.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，以太子左庶子鄭善果為山東道撫慰大使。

translations.literal: On the day yichou, [the court] appointed Zheng Shanguo, Left Associate of the Heir Apparent, as Pacification Commissioner of the Shandong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yichou, Zheng Shanguo, Left Associate of the Heir Apparent, was made Pacification Commissioner for the Shandong region.

sentences.zh: 世充將王德仁棄故洛陽城而遁，亞將趙季卿以城降。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong's general Wang Deren abandoned Old Luoyang and fled; Deputy General Zhao Jiqing surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Deren, a general under Wang Shichong, abandoned Old Luoyang and fled; Deputy General Zhao Jiqing surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 秦王世民囚竇建德、王琬、長孫安世、郭士衡等至洛陽城下，以示世充。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin, Shimin, brought Dou Jiande, Wang Wan, Changsun Anshi, Guo Shiheng, and others as prisoners to the foot of Luoyang's walls, to show Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin, Li Shimin, marched his prisoners—Dou Jiande, Wang Wan, Changsun Anshi, Guo Shiheng, and others—to the walls of Luoyang and displayed them to Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 世充與建德語而泣，仍遣安世等入城言敗狀。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong spoke with Dou Jiande and wept; he then sent Anshi and the others into the city to report the circumstances of defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong spoke with Dou Jiande and wept. Then he sent Anshi and the others back into the city to tell of their defeat.

sentences.zh: 世充召諸將議突圍，南走襄陽，諸將皆曰：「吾所恃者夏王，夏王今已為擒，雖得出，終必無成。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong summoned his generals to discuss breaking out and fleeing south to Xiangyang. All the generals said, "What we relied on was the King of Xia. The King of Xia has now been captured. Even if we get out, in the end we will surely accomplish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong called his generals together to discuss breaking out and fleeing south to Xiangyang. They all said, "What we counted on was the King of Xia. He is captured now. Even if we break out, we can never succeed in the end."

sentences.zh: 」丙寅，世充素服帥其太子、郡臣、二千餘人詣軍門降。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, Wang Shichong, in plain white dress, led his crown prince, the commandery officials, and more than two thousand people to the army gate to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingyin, Wang Shichong came to the army gate in mourning dress, leading his crown prince, his officials, and more than two thousand men to surrender.

sentences.zh: 世民禮接之，世充俯伏流汗。

translations.literal: Li Shimin received him with courtesy; Wang Shichong prostrated himself, sweating.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin received him with courtesy. Wang Shichong prostrated himself, drenched in sweat.

sentences.zh: 世民曰：「卿常以童子見處，今見童子，何恭之甚邪？

translations.literal: Li Shimin said, "You always treated me as a mere boy. Now you see this boy—why such excessive deference?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin said, "You always treated me as a mere boy. Now you see the boy—why bow so low?"

sentences.zh: 」世充頓首謝罪。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong knocked his head to the ground in apology.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong kowtowed in apology.

sentences.zh: 於是部分諸軍，先入洛陽，分守市肆，禁止侵掠，無敢犯者。

translations.literal: Thereupon he assigned the various armies, entered Luoyang first, posted guards at the markets and shops, forbade looting, and none dared violate the order.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin then deployed his forces, entered Luoyang first, posted guards at the markets, and forbade looting. No one dared violate the order.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，世民入宮城，命記室房玄齡先入中書、門下省收隋圖籍制詔，已為世充所毀，無所獲。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao, Li Shimin entered the palace city and ordered Recorder Fang Xuanling to go first into the Secretariat and the Chancellery to collect the Sui archives and edicts. They had already been destroyed by Wang Shichong, and nothing was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingmao, Li Shimin entered the palace city and ordered his recorder Fang Xuanling to go first to the Secretariat and Chancellery to recover the Sui archives and edicts. Wang Shichong had already destroyed them; nothing was found.

sentences.zh: 命蕭瑀、竇軌等封府庫，收其金帛，班賜將士。

translations.literal: He ordered Xiao Yu, Dou Gui, and others to seal the treasuries, collect the gold and silk, and distribute them among the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Xiao Yu, Dou Gui, and others to seal the treasuries, gather the gold and silk, and distribute them among the troops.

sentences.zh: 收世充之黨罪尤大者段達、王隆、崔洪丹、薛德音、楊汪、孟孝義、單雄信、楊公卿、郭什柱、郭士衡、董睿、張童兒、王德仁、朱粲、郭善才等十餘人斬於洛水之上。

translations.literal: More than ten of Wang Shichong's partisans whose crimes were greatest—Duan Da, Wang Long, Cui Hongdan, Xue Deyin, Yang Wang, Meng Xiaoyi, Shan Xiongxin, Yang Gongqing, Guo Shizhu, Guo Shiheng, Dong Rui, Zhang Tong'er, Wang Deren, Zhu Can, Guo Shancai, and others—were seized and executed on the bank of the Luo River.
translations.idiomatic: More than a dozen of Wang Shichong's followers whose crimes were gravest—among them Duan Da, Wang Long, Cui Hongdan, Xue Deyin, Yang Wang, Meng Xiaoyi, Shan Xiongxin, Yang Gongqing, Guo Shizhu, Guo Shiheng, Dong Rui, Zhang Tong'er, Wang Deren, Zhu Can, and Guo Shancai—were taken and beheaded on the bank of the Luo River.

sentences.zh: 初，李世勣與單雄信友善，誓同生死。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Shiji and Shan Xiongxin had been close friends and sworn to live and die together.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, Li Shiji and Shan Xiongxin had been close friends and sworn to live and die together.

sentences.zh: 及洛陽平，世勣言雄信驍健絕倫，請盡輸己之官爵以贖之，世民不許。

translations.literal: When Luoyang was pacified, Li Shiji said Shan Xiongxin was peerlessly brave and strong, and asked to surrender all his own offices and ranks to redeem him. Li Shimin would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell, Li Shiji said Shan Xiongxin was a warrior without equal and asked to give up all his own offices and honors to save him. Li Shimin refused.

sentences.zh: 世勣固請不能得，涕泣而退。

translations.literal: Li Shiji pressed his request insistently but could not obtain it; weeping, he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiji pleaded again and again, but could not move him. Weeping, he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 雄信曰：「我固知汝不辦事！

translations.literal: Shan Xiongxin said, "I knew all along you couldn't get things done!"
translations.idiomatic: Shan Xiongxin said, "I always knew you would never get this done!"

sentences.zh: 」世勣曰：「吾不惜餘生，與兄俱死；

translations.literal: Li Shiji said, "I do not begrudge the rest of my life; I would die with you, brother.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiji said, "I would not begrudge the rest of my life—I would die with you, brother.

sentences.zh: 但既以此身許國，事無兩遂。

translations.literal: But having already pledged this body to the state, both things cannot be fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: But I have already pledged this body to the state, and both courses cannot be taken at once.

sentences.zh: 且吾死之後，誰復視兄之妻子乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, after I die, who else will look after your wife and children?"
translations.idiomatic: And after I am dead, who will care for your wife and children?"

sentences.zh: 」乃割股肉以啖雄信，曰：「使此肉隨兄為土，庶幾猶不負昔誓也！

translations.literal: Thereupon he cut flesh from his thigh and fed it to Shan Xiongxin, saying, "Let this flesh turn to earth with you, brother—perhaps thus I still do not fail our old oath!"
translations.idiomatic: Then he cut flesh from his thigh and fed it to Shan Xiongxin, saying, "Let this flesh go into the earth with you, brother—then perhaps I will not have broken our old oath!"

sentences.zh: 」士民疾朱粲殘忍，競投瓦礫擊其屍，須臾如塚。

translations.literal: The people hated Zhu Can's cruelty and competed to throw tiles and stones at his corpse; in a moment it was like a mound.
translations.idiomatic: The people hated Zhu Can for his cruelty and pelted his corpse with tiles and stones until, in no time, it looked like a burial mound.

sentences.zh: 囚韋節、楊續、長孫安世等十餘人送長安。

translations.literal: Wei Jie, Yang Xu, Changsun Anshi, and more than ten other prisoners were sent to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jie, Yang Xu, Changsun Anshi, and more than ten other prisoners were sent to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 士民無罪為世充所囚者，皆釋之，所殺者祭而誄之。

translations.literal: Commoners and officials who had been imprisoned without guilt by Wang Shichong were all released; those he had killed were mourned with offerings and eulogized.
translations.idiomatic: Innocent townspeople and officials whom Wang Shichong had imprisoned were all released; those he had killed were mourned with sacrifices and eulogies.

sentences.zh: 初，秦王府屬杜如晦叔父淹事王世充。

translations.literal: Earlier, Du Yan, uncle of Du Ruhui of the Prince of Qin's staff, had served Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Du Yan—uncle of Du Ruhui, an officer on the Prince of Qin's staff—had served Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 淹素與如晦兄弟不協，譖如晦兄殺之，又囚其弟楚客，餓幾死，楚客終無怨色。

translations.literal: Du Yan had long been at odds with Du Ruhui and his brothers. He slandered Du Ruhui's elder brother and had him killed, and also imprisoned his younger brother Chuke, starving him nearly to death. Chuke never showed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yan had long been estranged from Du Ruhui and his brothers. He slandered Ruhui's elder brother until he was killed, then imprisoned the younger brother Chuke and starved him nearly to death. Chuke never showed a trace of resentment.

sentences.zh: 及洛陽平，淹當死，楚客涕泣請如晦救之，如晦不從。

translations.literal: When Luoyang was pacified, Du Yan was sentenced to death. Chuke wept and begged Du Ruhui to save him, but Du Ruhui would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell, Du Yan was condemned to die. Chuke wept and begged Du Ruhui to save him, but Ruhui refused.

sentences.zh: 楚客曰：「曩者叔已殺兄，今兄又殺叔，一門之內，自相殘而盡，豈不痛哉！

translations.literal: Chuke said, "Before, uncle killed elder brother; now elder brother kills uncle. Within one household, mutual slaughter until none remain—how is this not agonizing!"
translations.idiomatic: Chuke said, "Before, our uncle killed our elder brother; now our elder brother would kill our uncle. One household devouring itself until nothing is left—how can that not break the heart!"

sentences.zh: 」欲自剄，如晦乃為之請於世民，淹得免死。

translations.literal: About to cut his own throat, Du Ruhui then pleaded for him with Li Shimin, and Du Yan was spared death.
translations.idiomatic: On the verge of slitting his own throat, Chuke moved Du Ruhui to plead with Li Shimin, and Du Yan was spared execution.

sentences.zh: 秦王世民坐閶闔門，蘇威請見，稱老病不能拜。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin, Li Shimin, sat at the Changhe Gate. Su Wei requested an audience, claiming old age and illness and that he could not bow.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin, Li Shimin, took his seat at the Changhe Gate. Su Wei asked to see him, pleading old age and illness and saying he could not bow.

sentences.zh: 世民遣人數之曰：「公隋室宰相，危不能扶，使君弒國亡。

translations.literal: Li Shimin sent someone to rebuke him, saying, "You were a chancellor of the Sui house. In peril you could not support it, allowing the ruler to be assassinated and the state to perish.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin sent a messenger to rebuke him: "You were chancellor of the Sui. When the dynasty was in peril you did not save it, and the ruler was murdered and the realm lost.

sentences.zh: 見李密、王世充皆拜伏舞蹈。

translations.literal: When you saw Li Mi and Wang Shichong, you bowed prostrate and performed the ceremonial dance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when you saw Li Mi and Wang Shichong, you prostrated yourself and danced in submission.

sentences.zh: 今既老病，無勞相見。

translations.literal: Now that you are old and ill, there is no need to trouble with a meeting."
translations.idiomatic: Now that you are old and sick, there is no need for us to meet."

sentences.zh: 」及至長安，又請見，不許。

translations.literal: When he reached Chang'an, he again requested an audience, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: After he reached Chang'an, he asked to see Li Shimin again, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 既老且貧，無復官爵，卒於家，年八十二。

translations.literal: Old and poor, with no office or rank restored, he died at home at the age of eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Old, poor, and stripped of office and rank, he died at home at eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 秦王世民觀隋宮殿，歎曰：「逞侈心，窮人欲，無亡得乎！

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin, Li Shimin, viewed the Sui palaces and sighed, "Indulging extravagant hearts and exhausting human desire—could there be no ruin?"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin, Li Shimin, toured the Sui palaces and sighed, "To indulge every extravagance and exhaust every desire—how could ruin not follow?"

sentences.zh: 」命撤端門樓，焚乾陽殿，毀則天門及闕；

translations.literal: He ordered the Gate of Duan tower dismantled, the Qianyang Hall burned, and the Zetian Gate and its watchtower destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the tower of the Duan Gate torn down, the Qianyang Hall burned, and the Zetian Gate and its flanking towers demolished.

sentences.zh: 廢諸道場，城中僧尼，留有名德者各三十人，餘皆返初。

translations.literal: He abolished all Buddhist halls. Of the monks and nuns in the city, thirty each of those with renown and virtue were retained; the rest were sent back to lay life.
translations.idiomatic: He closed the Buddhist halls throughout the city. Of the monks and nuns there, thirty of the most eminent were kept; the rest were sent back to lay life.

sentences.zh: 前真定令周法明，法尚之弟也，隋末結客，襲據黃梅，遣族子孝節攻蘄春，兄子紹則攻安陸，子紹德攻沔陽，皆拔之。

translations.literal: Zhou Faming, former magistrate of Zhending and younger brother of Fa Shang, at the end of the Sui gathered adventurers, seized Huangmei by surprise, sent his clansman Xiaojie to attack Qichun, his brother's son Shaozze to attack Anlu, and his son Shaode to attack Mianyang—all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Faming, formerly magistrate of Zhending and younger brother of Fa Shang, had at the end of the Sui gathered fighting men, seized Huangmei by surprise, and sent his clansman Xiaojie against Qichun, his brother's son Shaozze against Anlu, and his own son Shaode against Mianyang—all of which fell to him.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以四郡來降。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, he submitted the four commanderies in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengwu, he surrendered four commanderies to Tang.

sentences.zh: 壬申，齊善行以洺、相、魏等州來降。

translations.literal: On the day renshen, Qi Shanxing submitted Mo, Xiang, Wei, and other prefectures in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renshen, Qi Shanxing surrendered Mo, Xiang, Wei, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 時建德餘眾走至洺州，欲立建德養子為主，徵兵以拒唐；

translations.literal: At the time, Dou Jiande's remnant troops had fled to Mozhou, wishing to install Jiande's adopted son as ruler and levy troops to resist Tang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, the remnants of Dou Jiande's army had fled to Mozhou. They wanted to set up Jiande's adopted son as their leader and raise troops to resist Tang.

sentences.zh: 又欲剽掠居民，還向海隅為盜。

translations.literal: They also wished to plunder the populace and return to the coastal margins to become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Others wanted to plunder the people and retreat to the coast to live as bandits.

sentences.zh: 善行獨以為不可，曰：「隋末喪亂，故吾屬相聚草野，苟求生耳。

translations.literal: Qi Shanxing alone thought this impossible and said, "At the end of the Sui there was chaos and ruin, so our group gathered in the wilds, merely seeking to survive.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shanxing alone objected. He said, "At the end of the Sui there was chaos and ruin, and we gathered in the wild merely to survive.

sentences.zh: 以夏王之英武，平定河朔，士馬精強，一朝為擒，易如反掌，豈非天命有所屬，非人力所能爭邪！

translations.literal: With the King of Xia's heroic martial prowess, he pacified Heshuo; his troops and horses were elite and strong. Yet he was captured in a single morning, easy as turning one's palm—is this not proof that Heaven's mandate has its allotted recipient, and not something human effort can contest?"
translations.idiomatic: The King of Xia was heroic and martial; he pacified Heshuo, and his men and horses were the finest in the land. Yet he was captured in a morning, as easily as turning one's hand—is that not Heaven choosing its master, beyond anything human strength can fight?"

sentences.zh: 今喪敗如此，守亦無成，逃亦不免；

translations.literal: Now, defeated and ruined like this, to hold out achieves nothing, and to flee is not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Now we are broken like this. To hold out is hopeless; to flee is no escape.

sentences.zh: 等為亡國，豈可復遺毒於民！

translations.literal: Alike we are a defeated state—how can we again leave poison among the people!"
translations.idiomatic: We are already a fallen cause in any case—how can we visit more harm on the people!"

sentences.zh: 不若委心請命於唐。

translations.literal: Better to surrender our hearts and plead for orders from Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Better to submit wholeheartedly and accept Tang's command.

sentences.zh: 必欲得繒帛者，當盡散府庫之物，勿復殘民也！

translations.literal: If silk and cloth must be had, we should exhaust the treasury stores in distribution and not again harm the people!"
translations.idiomatic: If you must have silk and cloth, take everything in the treasury and give it out—do not prey on the people again!"

sentences.zh: 」於是運府庫之帛數十萬段，置萬春宮東街，以散將卒，凡三晝夜乃畢。

translations.literal: Thereupon they moved several hundred thousand bolts of cloth from the treasury, placed them on East Street of Wanchun Palace, and distributed them to the officers and soldiers. It took three days and nights to finish.
translations.idiomatic: So they hauled several hundred thousand bolts of cloth from the treasury to East Street of Wanchun Palace and handed them out to officers and soldiers. The distribution took three days and three nights to complete.

sentences.zh: 仍佈兵守坊巷，得物者即出，無得更入人家。

translations.literal: They still deployed troops to guard the lanes and alleys; those who had obtained goods had to leave at once and were not permitted to enter anyone's home again.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers remained posted in every lane and alley. Anyone who had looted something had to surrender it and leave immediately—no second raids into private houses.

sentences.zh: 士卒散盡，然後與右僕射裴矩、行臺曹旦，帥其百官奉建德妻曹氏及傳國八璽，並破宇文化及所得珍寶，請降於唐。

translations.literal: After the soldiers had all scattered, he then joined Right Vice Director Pei Ju and Regional Headquarters Chief Cao Dan, leading all his officials to present Dou Jiande's wife Lady Cao, the eight imperial seals of transmission, and the precious treasures taken when Yuwen Huaji was defeated, and requested surrender to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Only after his troops had fully dispersed did he go with Pei Ju, the Right Vice Director, and Cao Dan, chief of the regional headquarters, at the head of the whole court to offer up Dou Jiande's wife, Lady Cao, the eight seals of state, and the treasures seized from Yuwen Huaji—then sue for peace with Tang.

sentences.zh: 上以善行為秦王左二護軍，仍厚賜之。

translations.literal: The Emperor appointed Shanxing as the Prince of Qin's Left Second Protector-General and again rewarded him generously.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor made Shanxing Left Second Protector-General under the Prince of Qin and heaped rewards upon him.

sentences.zh: 初，竇建德之誅宇文化及也，隋南陽公主有子曰禪師，建德虎賁郎將於士澄問之曰：「化及大逆，兄弟之子皆當從坐，若不能捨禪師，當相為留之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Dou Jiande was executing Yuwen Huaji, the Sui Princess of Nanyang had a son named Chanshi. Jiande's Tiger Vanguard officer Yu Shicheng asked him, saying, "Huaji committed great treason; the sons of his brothers should all be punished as accessories. If you cannot abandon Chanshi, we should keep him together."
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande put Yuwen Huaji to death, the Sui Princess of Nanyang still had a young son, Chanshi. Yu Shicheng, a Tiger Vanguard officer in Jiande's service, asked him: "Huaji's crime was capital treason—his brothers' sons should all die with him. If you cannot bring yourself to abandon Chanshi, let us hide him together."

sentences.zh: 」公主泣曰：「虎賁既隋室貴臣，茲事何須見問！

translations.literal: The princess wept and said, "The Tiger Vanguard are noble ministers of the Sui house—why need you even ask about this!"
translations.idiomatic: The princess wept. "You Tiger Vanguard are honored servants of the Sui. Why do you even put such a question to me?"

sentences.zh: 」建德竟殺之。

translations.literal: Jiande nevertheless killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande killed the boy anyway.

sentences.zh: 公主尋請為尼。

translations.literal: The princess soon requested to become a nun.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, the princess asked to take the veil.

sentences.zh: 及建德敗，公主將歸長安，與宇文士及遇於洛陽，士及請與相見，公主不可。

translations.literal: When Jiande was defeated, as the princess was about to return to Chang'an, she encountered Yuwen Shiji in Luoyang. Shiji asked to see her; the princess refused.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiande's fall, the princess was on her way back to Chang'an when she met Yuwen Shiji in Luoyang. He begged for an audience; she would not grant it.

sentences.zh: 士及立於戶外，請復為夫婦。

translations.literal: Shiji stood outside the door and asked to resume their marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji waited at the threshold and pleaded that they become husband and wife again.

sentences.zh: 公主曰：「我與君仇家，今所以不手刃君者，但謀逆之日，察君不預知耳。

translations.literal: The princess said, "You and I are from feuding houses. The reason I do not kill you with my own hand today is only that, on the day the plot was laid, I saw you had no foreknowledge of it."
translations.idiomatic: The princess said, "Our families are sworn enemies. The only reason I do not cut you down myself is that, when the treason was plotted, I could see you were not in on it."

sentences.zh: 」訶令速去。

translations.literal: She berated him and ordered him to leave at once.
translations.idiomatic: She scolded him and told him to be gone immediately.

sentences.zh: 士及固請，公主怒曰：「必欲就死，可相見也！

translations.literal: Shiji pressed his request insistently. The princess angrily said, "If you are determined to die, then you may see me!"
translations.idiomatic: Shiji would not desist. The princess flared: "If you are bent on dying, come in and see me!"

sentences.zh: 」士及知不可屈，乃拜辭而去。

translations.literal: Shiji knew she could not be moved, so he bowed in farewell and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing she would not yield, Shiji bowed his farewell and left.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，以周法明為黃州總管。

translations.literal: On yihai day, Zhou Faming was appointed Regional Commander of Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yihai, Zhou Faming was made regional commander of Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，王世充徐州行臺杞王世辯以徐、宋等三十八州詣河南道安撫大使任□襄請降；

translations.literal: On wuyin day, Wang Shibian of Qi, regional headquarters chief at Xuzhou under Wang Shichong, brought thirty-eight prefectures including Xu and Song to submit surrender to Henan Circuit Pacification Commissioner Ren □xiang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Wang Shibian of Qi—Wang Shichong's Xuzhou headquarters chief—surrendered thirty-eight prefectures, Xu and Song among them, to Ren □xiang, Pacification Commissioner of the Henan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 世充故地悉平。

translations.literal: All of Shichong's former territory was completely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Every district that had belonged to Shichong was now subdued.

sentences.zh: 竇建德博州刺史馮士羨復推淮安王神通為慰撫山東使，徇下三十餘州；

translations.literal: Feng Shixian, prefect of Bozhou under Dou Jiande, again installed Prince Huai'an Li Shentong as Commissioner to Pacify and Comfort Shandong, and subjugated more than thirty prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Shixian, Dou Jiande's prefect of Bozhou, once more raised Prince Huai'an Li Shentong as Commissioner to Pacify Shandong and brought more than thirty prefectures to heel.

sentences.zh: 建德之地悉平。

translations.literal: All of Jiande's territory was completely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande's former domains were wholly pacified.

sentences.zh: 己卯，代州總管李大恩擊苑君璋，破之。

translations.literal: On jimao day, Daizhou Regional Commander Li Da'en attacked Yuan Junzhang and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, Li Da'en, regional commander of Daizhou, routed Yuan Junzhang.

sentences.zh: 突厥寇邊，長平靖王叔良督五將擊之，叔良中流矢；

translations.literal: The Turks raided the frontier. Prince Changpingjing Li Shuliang supervised five generals in attacking them, and Shuliang was struck by a flying arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Turks struck the border. Prince Changpingjing Li Shuliang took five generals against them and took an arrow in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 師旋，六月，戊子，卒於道。

translations.literal: On the army's return, in the sixth month, on wuzi day, he died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The column was marching home when, in the sixth month on wuzi, he died on the road.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，孟海公餘黨蔣善合以鄆州，孟啖鬼以曹州來降。

translations.literal: On wuxu day, Jiang Shanhe, a remnant of Duke Meng Hai, came to surrender with Yanzhou, and Meng Dangui with Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Jiang Shanhe—of Duke Meng Hai's lingering faction—surrendered Yanzhou, and Meng Dangui surrendered Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 啖鬼，海公之從兄也。

translations.literal: Dangui was Duke Hai's elder cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Dangui was a first cousin, once removed, of Duke Hai.

sentences.zh: 庚子，營州人石世則執總管晉文衍，舉州叛，奉靺鞨突地稽為主。

translations.literal: On gengzi day, Shize of Yingzhou seized Regional Commander Jin Wenyian, raised the whole prefecture in rebellion, and installed the Mohe leader Tudi Ji as their lord.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, a man of Yingzhou named Shize arrested its regional commander Jin Wenyian, rebelled with the entire prefecture, and set up the Mohe chieftain Tudi Ji as ruler.

sentences.zh: 黃州總管周法明攻蕭銑安州，拔之，獲其總管馬貴遷。

translations.literal: Huangzhou Regional Commander Zhou Faming attacked Anzhou, held by Xiao Xuan, captured it, and took its regional commander Ma Guiqian prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Faming of Huangzhou stormed Xiao Xuan's Anzhou, took the city, and captured its commander Ma Guiqian.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以右驍衛將軍盛彥師為宋州總管，安撫河南。

translations.literal: On yisi day, Right Xiaowei Guard General Sheng Yanshi was appointed Songzhou Regional Commander to pacify Henan.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Sheng Yanshi, general of the Right Xiaowei Guard, was made regional commander of Songzhou with charge over pacifying Henan.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，海州賊帥臧君相以五州來降，拜海州總管。

translations.literal: On yimao day, bandit chief of Haizhou Zang Junxiang came to surrender with five prefectures and was appointed Haizhou Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Zang Junxiang, rebel leader of Haizhou, submitted five prefectures and was enfeoffed as Haizhou's regional commander.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，庚申，王世充行臺王弘烈、王泰、左僕射豆盧行褒、右僕射蘇世長以襄州來降。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on gengshen day, Wang Shichong's regional headquarters chiefs Wang Honglie and Wang Tai, Left Vice Director Doulu Xingbao, and Right Vice Director Su Shichang surrendered Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, seventh month, gengshen: Wang Honglie and Wang Tai of Shichong's headquarters, with Left Vice Director Doulu Xingbao and Right Vice Director Su Shichang, surrendered Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 上與行褒、世長皆有舊，先是，屢以書招之，行褒輒殺使者；

translations.literal: The Emperor had old ties with both Xingbao and Shichang. Earlier he had repeatedly sent letters summoning them, but Xingbao always killed the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor and both Xingbao and Shichang went back a long way. He had written again and again urging them to come over; Xingbao kept murdering the messengers.

sentences.zh: 既至長安，上誅行褒而責世長。

translations.literal: Once they reached Chang'an, the Emperor executed Xingbao and reproached Shichang.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived in Chang'an, the Emperor put Xingbao to death and took Shichang to task.

sentences.zh: 世長曰：「隋失其鹿，天下共逐之。

translations.literal: Shichang said, "Sui lost the deer, and all under Heaven joined in the chase."
translations.idiomatic: Shichang said, "When Sui lost the prize, the whole realm ran to hunt it."

sentences.zh: 陛下既得之矣，豈可復忿同獵之徒，問爭肉之罪乎！

translations.literal: "Your Majesty has already obtained it—how can you still bear resentment toward fellow hunters and inquire into the crime of competing for the meat!"
