translations.idiomatic: "Now that Your Majesty holds it, will you still rage at those who hunted beside you and call them to account for quarreling over the kill?"

sentences.zh: 」上笑而釋之，以為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and released him, appointing him Remonstrance and Discussion Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor laughed, let the matter drop, and made him Remonstrance and Discussion Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 嘗從校獵高陵，大獲禽獸，上顧群臣曰：「今日畋，樂乎？

translations.literal: Once, accompanying a hunting expedition at Gaoling, they took many birds and beasts. The Emperor turned to his ministers and said, "Today's hunt—are you pleased?"
translations.idiomatic: On a hunt at Gaoling they bagged game in abundance. The Emperor looked at his court and asked, "Was today's sport enjoyable?"

sentences.zh: 」世長對曰：「陛下遊獵，薄廢萬機，不滿十旬，未足為樂！

translations.literal: Shichang replied, "Your Majesty's excursions for hunting lightly set aside the myriad affairs of state. Not even ten days have passed—this is hardly enough to be called pleasure!"
translations.idiomatic: Shichang answered, "Your Majesty's hunting trips barely touch the myriad burdens of rule. Less than a hundred days in, and already you call this joy?"

sentences.zh: 」上變色，既而笑曰：「狂態復發邪？

translations.literal: The Emperor's expression changed; then he laughed and said, "Has your wild manner broken out again?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's face darkened—then he laughed. "Your mad streak is back, is it?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「於臣則狂，於陛下甚忠。

translations.literal: He replied, "Wild for me, but most loyal toward Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: "Madness in me, perhaps—but toward Your Majesty, utmost loyalty."

sentences.zh: 」嘗侍宴披香殿，酒酣，謂上曰：「此殿煬帝之所為邪？

translations.literal: Once, while attending a banquet in Pixiang Hall, when the wine had warmed him, he said to the Emperor, "Was this hall built by Emperor Yang?"
translations.idiomatic: At another time, feasting in Pixiang Hall with wine in his blood, he asked the Emperor, "Did Emperor Yang build this hall?"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「卿諫似直而實多詐，豈不知此殿朕所為，而謂之煬帝乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Your remonstrance seems straight but is in fact much deception—do you not know that I built this hall, yet call it Emperor Yang's?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "You sound blunt, but this is mostly theater. You know perfectly well I built this hall—why pretend it was Yang's?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣實不知，但見其華侈如傾宮、鹿臺，非興王之所為故也。

translations.literal: He replied, "Your subject truly did not know; I only saw that its splendor and extravagance resemble the Tilted Palace and the Deer Terrace—not what a founding king would do."
translations.idiomatic: "I truly did not know," he said. "I saw only that it is as lavish as the Tilted Palace and the Deer Terrace—hardly the work of a king who is raising a new age."

sentences.zh: 若陛下為之，誠非所宜。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty built it, it truly would not be fitting.
translations.idiomatic: If it was Your Majesty who built it, then it is truly unfitting.

sentences.zh: 臣昔侍陛下於武功，見所居宅僅庇風雨，當時亦以為足。

translations.literal: "When your subject once attended Your Majesty at Wugong, I saw the dwelling where you lived barely kept out wind and rain—and even then you considered it sufficient."
translations.idiomatic: "When I served you at Wugong, your house scarcely kept off wind and rain—and even then you called it enough."

sentences.zh: 今因隋之宮室，已極侈矣，而又增之，將何以矯其失乎？

translations.literal: "Now, inheriting Sui's palaces, they are already the height of extravagance—and you add to them still. How then will you correct their faults?"
translations.idiomatic: "Today you have Sui's palaces, already extravagance itself, and you enlarge them further. How will you ever correct the old excess?"

sentences.zh: 」上深然之。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply agreed with this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was deeply persuaded.

sentences.zh: 甲子，秦王世民至長安。

translations.literal: On jiazi day, the Prince of Qin Shimin arrived at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Prince of Qin Shimin entered Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 世民被黃金甲，齊王元吉、李世勣等二十五將從其後，鐵騎萬匹，甲士三萬人，前後部鼓吹，俘王世充、竇建德及隋乘輿、御物獻於太廟，行飲至之禮以饗之。

translations.literal: Shimin wore golden armor; the Prince of Qi Yuanji, Li Shiji, and twenty-five other generals followed behind; ten thousand iron cavalry and thirty thousand armored soldiers; front and rear guard musicians; captives Wang Shichong and Dou Jiande, along with the Sui imperial carriage and regalia, were presented at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the rite of drinking upon arrival was performed to feast them.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin rode in golden armor, with Prince of Qi Yuanji, Li Shiji, and twenty-five other generals behind him; ten thousand iron horses and thirty thousand armored men; ceremonial music before and behind. Wang Shichong and Dou Jiande, the Sui imperial carriage and regalia, were offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the victory feast of return was celebrated.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，高句麗王建武遣使入貢。

translations.literal: On yichou day, King Jianwu of Goguryeo sent envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, King Jianwu of Goguryeo sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 建武，元之弟也。

translations.literal: Jianwu was Yuan's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu was the younger brother of Yuan.

sentences.zh: 上見王世充而數之，世充曰：「臣罪固當誅，然秦王許臣不死。

translations.literal: The Emperor saw Wang Shichong and reproached him. Shichong said, "Your subject's crime indeed deserves execution, yet the Prince of Qin promised me I would not die."
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor confronted Wang Shichong, Shichong said, "I deserve death—that is certain. But the Prince of Qin promised my life."

sentences.zh: 」丙寅，詔赦世充為庶人，與兄弟子侄徙處蜀；

translations.literal: On bingyin day, an edict pardoned Shichong as a commoner, and he was relocated to Shu with his brothers, nephews, and cousins.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, an edict spared Shichong's life and reduced him to commoner status; he and his brothers, nephews, and cousins were sent into exile in Shu.

sentences.zh: 斬竇建德於市。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande was executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande was beheaded in public.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以天下略定，大赦。

translations.literal: On dingmao, because the realm was largely pacified, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao day, with the empire largely settled, the court declared a grand amnesty.

sentences.zh: 百姓給復一年。

translations.literal: The common people were granted one year of tax and corvée relief.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes and labor levies were remitted for the people for one year.

sentences.zh: 陝、鼎、函、虢、虞、芮六州，轉輸勞費，幽州管內，久隔寇戎，並給復二年。

translations.literal: The six prefectures of Shaan, Ding, Han, Guo, Yu, and Rui, worn out by transport and supply burdens, and the territory within Youzhou, long cut off by bandits and raiders, were all granted two years of relief.
translations.idiomatic: Shaan, Ding, Han, Guo, Yu, and Rui—the six prefectures exhausted by relay transport—and Youzhou, long isolated by enemy incursions, received two years of remission.

sentences.zh: 律、令、格、式，且用開皇舊制。

translations.literal: For statutes, ordinances, regulations, and forms, the former Kaihuang system was temporarily used.
translations.idiomatic: The legal codes—statutes, orders, precedents, and administrative formulas—were for the time being restored to the Kaihuang-era framework.

sentences.zh: 赦令既下，而王、竇餘黨尚有遠徙者，治書侍御史孫伏伽上言：「兵、食可去，信不可去，陛下已赦而復徙之，是自違本心，使臣民何所憑依？

translations.literal: After the amnesty decree had been issued, yet among the remaining partisans of Wang and Dou there were still those being banished to distant places. Supervising Secretary Sun Fuga submitted a memorial: "Arms and provisions may be dispensed with, but trust cannot be dispensed with. Your Majesty has already granted amnesty yet again banishes them—this is to go against your own heart. What shall officials and people rely upon?"
translations.idiomatic: The amnesty had barely been promulgated when partisans of Wang and Dou were still being sent into distant exile. Supervising Secretary Sun Fuga memorialized the throne: "One may do without arms and grain, but not without good faith. Having pardoned these men, Your Majesty now banishes them again—you contradict your own intent. On what, then, may your subjects depend?"

sentences.zh: 且世充尚蒙寬宥，況於餘黨，所宜縱釋。

translations.literal: Moreover, Shichong still received leniency; how much more so the remaining partisans—it is fitting to release them.
translations.idiomatic: If even Shichong was shown mercy, his followers ought all the more to be set free.

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 王世充以防夫未備，置雍州廨捨。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong, because defensive laborers were not yet ready, was lodged in the offices of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong was quartered in the Yongzhou administrative compound, as the conscript guards were not yet in place.

sentences.zh: 獨孤機之子定州刺史修德帥兄弟至其所，矯稱敕呼鄭王；

translations.literal: Xiude, son of Dugu Ji and governor of Dingzhou, led his brothers to his place and falsely claimed an imperial order summoning the Prince of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiude, son of Dugu Ji and governor of Dingzhou, went with his brothers to Wang's quarters and, forging an imperial summons, called for the Prince of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 世充與兄世惲趨出，修德等殺之。

translations.literal: Shichong and his elder brother Shiyun hurried out; Xiude and the others killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong and his elder brother Shiyun rushed out—and Xiude and his men cut them down.

sentences.zh: 詔免修德官。

translations.literal: An edict stripped Xiude of his office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed Xiude from his post.

sentences.zh: 其餘兄弟子侄等，於道亦以謀反誅。

translations.literal: The rest of the brothers, sons, and nephews were also executed on the road on charges of plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: His remaining brothers, sons, and nephews were likewise put to death on the road, condemned for treason.

sentences.zh: 隋末錢幣濫薄，至裁皮糊紙為之，民間不勝其弊。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui, coinage was debased and thin; it reached the point of cutting leather and pasting paper to make it—the people could not bear the harm.
translations.idiomatic: By the Sui dynasty's end, currency had grown so debased that people were cutting leather and gluing paper into coins; the common folk could scarcely endure the misery of it.

sentences.zh: 至是，初行開元通寶錢，逕八分，重二銖四參，積十錢重一兩，輕重大小最為折衷，遠近便之。

translations.literal: At this time, the Kaiyuan Tongbao coin was first issued, one cun eight fen in diameter, weighing two zhu and four candareens; ten coins accumulated weighed one liang—the weight and size were the most balanced compromise, convenient near and far.
translations.idiomatic: At this juncture the Kaiyuan Tongbao was introduced for the first time: eight fen in diameter, two zhu and four candareens in weight; ten coins stacked to one liang—a measure of weight and size judged the most practical balance, welcomed alike near and far.

sentences.zh: 命給事中歐陽詢撰其文並書，迴環可讀。

translations.literal: He ordered Supervising Secretary Ouyang Xun to compose the inscription and write it; read in circuit it could be read.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xun, a supervising secretary, was commissioned to draft and calligraph the legend—a phrase that reads the same whether traced in a circle.

sentences.zh: 以屈突通為陝東道大行臺右僕射，鎮洛陽；

translations.literal: Qu Tuo was appointed Right Vice Director of the Grand Eastern Shaan Circuit Commissioner, stationed at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Tuo was made Right Vice Director of the Eastern Shaan Grand Traveling Platform and posted to guard Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 以淮陽王道玄為洛州總管，李世勣父蓋竟無恙而還，詔復其官爵。

translations.literal: Prince of Huaiyang Daoxuan was made Governor-General of Luozhou; Li Shiji's father Gai returned ultimately unharmed, and an edict restored his rank and title.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Huaiyang, Daoxuan, was appointed Governor-General of Luozhou; Li Shiji's father Gai at last returned unharmed, and an edict restored his offices and titles.

sentences.zh: 竇軌還益州。

translations.literal: Dou Gui returned to Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Gui went back to Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 軌將兵征討，或經旬月不解甲。

translations.literal: When Gui led troops on punitive campaigns, sometimes for ten days or a month he would not remove his armor.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Gui took the field, he sometimes went ten days or a full month without doffing his armor.

sentences.zh: 性嚴酷，將佐有犯，無貴賤立斬之，鞭撻吏民，常流血滿庭，所部重足屏息。

translations.literal: By nature severe and cruel, if officers and aides committed offenses, regardless of noble or humble he immediately beheaded them; he flogged officials and people until blood often filled the courtyard—the region under his command walked on tiptoes and held their breath.
translations.idiomatic: Harsh by nature, he beheaded offending officers on the spot, high or low alike; he flogged officials and commoners until blood pooled in the courtyard, and all who served under him lived in dread, scarcely daring to breathe.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，置錢監於洛、並、幽、益等諸州，秦王世民、齊王元吉賜三爐，裴寂賜一爐，聽鑄錢。

translations.literal: On guiyou, mint supervisors were established in Luoyang, Bing, You, Yi, and other prefectures; Prince of Qin Shimin and Prince of Qi Yuanji were granted three furnaces each, Pei Ji one furnace, permitted to cast coin.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day, mints were established at Luoyang, Bing, You, Yi, and other prefectures; the Prince of Qin, Shimin, and the Prince of Qi, Yuanji, were each granted three furnaces, Pei Ji one, and authorized to cast coin.

sentences.zh: 自餘敢盜鑄者，身死，家口配沒。

translations.literal: Henceforth, whoever dared illicitly cast coin—death to the person, household members distributed as slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone else who dared counterfeit coin would be executed, and his household enslaved.

sentences.zh: 河北既平，上以陳君賓為洺州刺史。

translations.literal: Once Hebei was pacified, the Emperor appointed Chen Junbin Governor of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: With Hebei pacified, the emperor named Chen Junbin governor of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 將軍秦武通等將兵屯洺州，欲使分鎮東方諸州；

translations.literal: General Qin Wutong and others stationed troops at Mingzhou, intending to have them garrison separately the eastern prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: General Qin Wutong and others encamped at Mingzhou, intending to detach forces to garrison the eastern prefectures.

sentences.zh: 又以鄭善果等為慰撫大使，就洺州選補山東州縣官。

translations.literal: Also appointing Zheng Shanguo and others as pacification commissioners, from Mingzhou selecting and filling posts for Shandong prefecture and county officials.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Shanguo and others were also appointed pacification commissioners and, operating from Mingzhou, were to select and install officials for the prefectures and counties of the east.

sentences.zh: 竇建德之敗也，其諸將多盜匿庫物，及居閭里，暴橫為民患，唐官吏以法繩之，或加捶撻，建德故將皆驚懼不安。

translations.literal: When Dou Jiande was defeated, many of his generals had stolen and concealed treasury goods; when they lived among the neighborhoods they were violent and oppressive, a affliction to the people. Tang officials restrained them by law, sometimes adding beatings—all of Jiande's former generals were alarmed and uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: After Dou Jiande's defeat, many of his generals had looted and hidden treasury goods; back among the townsfolk they bullied and preyed on the people. Tang magistrates held them to the law, sometimes with the lash—and Jiande's old commanders grew fearful and restless.

sentences.zh: 高雅賢、王小胡家在洺州，欲竊其家以逃，官吏捕之，雅賢等亡命至貝州。

translations.literal: Gao Yaxian and Wang Xiaohu had homes in Mingzhou; wishing to raid their households to flee, officials arrested them—Yaxian and others fled as outlaws to Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yaxian and Wang Xiaohu, whose families were in Mingzhou, planned to plunder their homes and flee; officials moved to seize them, and Yaxian and his companions escaped as fugitives to Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 會上征建德故將范願、董康買、曹湛及雅賢等，於是願等相謂曰：「王世充以洛陽降唐，其將相大臣段達、單雄信等皆夷滅；

translations.literal: Just then the Emperor summoned Jiande's former generals Fan Yuan, Dong Kangmai, Cao Zhan, and Yaxian and others. Thereupon Yuan and the others said to one another: "Wang Shichong surrendered Luoyang to Tang, yet his generals, chancellors, and great ministers Duan Da, Shan Xiongxin, and others were all exterminated."
translations.idiomatic: Just then the court summoned Jiande's former generals—Fan Yuan, Dong Kangmai, Cao Zhan, Yaxian, and the rest. Yuan and his companions said to one another: "When Wang Shichong surrendered Luoyang to Tang, his generals and ministers—Duan Da, Shan Xiongxin, and the rest—were all put to the sword."

sentences.zh: 吾屬至長安，必不免矣。

translations.literal: When our sort reach Chang'an, we surely cannot escape.
translations.idiomatic: If we go to Chang'an, we will not be spared.

sentences.zh: 吾屬自十年以來，身經百戰，當死久矣，今何惜餘生，不以之立事。

translations.literal: Our sort, since ten years ago, have personally endured a hundred battles—we ought to have died long ago. Why now cherish remaining life and not use it to accomplish something?
translations.idiomatic: For ten years we have fought a hundred battles—we should have died long ago. Why cling to what life remains instead of risking it for a cause?

sentences.zh: 且夏王得淮安王，遇以客禮，唐得夏王即殺之。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the Prince of Xia obtained the Prince of Huai'an, he treated him with guest rites; when Tang obtained the Prince of Xia, they immediately killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Xia captured the Prince of Huai'an, he received him as an honored guest; when Tang took the Prince of Xia, they killed him at once.

sentences.zh: 吾屬皆為夏王所厚，今不為之報仇，將無以見天下之士！

translations.literal: We have all been treated generously by the Prince of Xia—if we do not now avenge him, how shall we face the gentlemen of the realm!
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xia treated us all with great favor—if we fail to avenge him now, how can we ever face honorable men under heaven!

sentences.zh: 」乃謀作亂，卜之，以劉氏為主吉，因相與之漳南，見建德故將劉雅，以其謀告之。

translations.literal: They then plotted rebellion; divining, taking a Liu as leader was auspicious. Accordingly they went together to Zhangnan, saw Jiande's former general Liu Ya, and told him their plan.
translations.idiomatic: They resolved on rebellion. Divination showed that a Liu should lead them, so they went together to Zhangnan, sought out Jiande's former general Liu Ya, and confided their design.

sentences.zh: 雅曰：「天下適安定，吾將老於耕桑，不願復起兵！

translations.literal: Ya said: "The realm has just been settled—I intend to grow old in farming and mulberry; I do not wish to raise troops again!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ya replied: "The realm has only just found peace. I mean to live out my days tilling fields and tending mulberry—I have no wish to take up arms again!"

sentences.zh: 」眾怒，且恐洩其謀，遂殺之。

translations.literal: The crowd grew angry, and fearing he would leak their plot, they killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, and fearing he would betray them, they killed him.

sentences.zh: 故漢東公劉黑闥，時屏居漳南，諸將往詣之，告以其謀，黑闥欣然從之。

translations.literal: The former Duke of Handong Liu Heita was then living in seclusion at Zhangnan; the generals went to visit him, told him their plot, and Heita gladly joined.
translations.idiomatic: The former Duke of Handong, Liu Heita, was then living in retirement at Zhangnan. The generals sought him out, disclosed their plan, and Heita gladly agreed.

sentences.zh: 黑闥方種蔬，即殺耕牛，與之共飲食定計，聚眾得百人。

translations.literal: Heita was just planting vegetables; he immediately slaughtered the plow ox, shared food and drink with them to fix the plan, gathered a crowd amounting to a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Heita had been planting vegetables; he at once slaughtered his plow ox, feasted with them to settle their plan, and mustered a band of a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，襲漳南縣據之。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, they raided Zhangnan County and seized it.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day they stormed Zhangnan County and took it.

sentences.zh: 是時，諸道有事則置行臺尚書省，無事則罷之。

translations.literal: At this time, when a circuit had business to attend to a Traveling Platform Secretariat was established; when there was none, it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, whenever a circuit faced urgent affairs a Traveling Platform Secretariat was set up; when the crisis passed, it was dissolved.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞黑闥作亂，乃置山東道行臺於洺州，魏、冀、定、滄並置總管府。

translations.literal: When the court heard Heita had risen in rebellion, it established the Shandong Circuit Traveling Platform at Mingzhou; Wei, Ji, Ding, and Cang each had a Governor-General's office established.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Heita's revolt, the court established a Shandong Circuit Traveling Platform at Mingzhou and set up governor-general offices in Wei, Ji, Ding, and Cang.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以淮安王神通為山東道臺右僕射。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Prince of Huai'an Shentong was made Right Vice Director of the Shandong Circuit Platform.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingchou day, the Prince of Huai'an, Shentong, was appointed Right Vice Director of the Shandong Circuit Platform.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，褒州道安撫使郭行方攻蕭銑鄀州，拔之。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Bao Circuit Pacification Commissioner Guo Xingfang attacked Xiao Xian's E Prefecture and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day, Guo Xingfang, pacification commissioner of the Bao circuit, attacked E Prefecture, held by Xiao Xian, and took it.

sentences.zh: 孟海公與竇建德同伏誅，戴州刺史孟□敢鬼不自安，挾海公之子義以曹、戴二州反，以禹城令蔣善合為腹心；

translations.literal: Meng Haigong was executed together with Dou Jiande. Dai Prefecture Governor Meng□ Gan Gui, ill at ease, took Haigong's son Yi and rebelled with Cao and Dai prefectures, making Yucheng Magistrate Jiang Shanhe his trusted confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Haigong was executed along with Dou Jiande. Meng□ Gan Gui, governor of Dai Prefecture, unsettled by events, raised Cao and Dai in rebellion with Haigong's son Yi, and made Jiang Shanhe, magistrate of Yucheng, his closest adviser.

sentences.zh: 善合與其左右同謀斬之。

translations.literal: Shanhe, together with his attendants, conspired together and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shanhe and his men plotted together and cut him down.

sentences.zh: 八月，丙戌朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the first day of bingxu, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the first day of the bingxu cycle, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，命太子安撫北邊。

translations.literal: On dinghai, the Crown Prince was ordered to pacify the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: On the dinghai day, the crown prince was charged with pacifying the northern border.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，劉黑闥陷鄃縣，魏州刺史權威、貝州刺史戴元祥與戰，皆敗死，黑闥悉收其餘眾及器械。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Liu Heita captured Yu County; Wei Prefecture Governor Quan Wei and Beizhou Prefecture Governor Dai Yuanxiang fought him, both were defeated and died; Heita gathered all their remaining troops and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day, Liu Heita took Yu County. Quan Wei, governor of Wei Prefecture, and Dai Yuanxiang, governor of Beizhou, gave battle and were both defeated and killed; Heita absorbed their remaining troops and arms.

sentences.zh: 竇建德舊黨稍稍出歸之，眾至二千人，為壇於漳南，祭建德，告以舉兵之意，自稱大將軍。

translations.literal: Jiande's old partisans gradually came out to join him; the host reached two thousand. They built an altar at Zhangnan, sacrificed to Jiande, declared their intent to raise arms, and Heita styled himself Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande's old followers drifted in one after another until his force reached two thousand. At Zhangnan they raised an altar, offered sacrifice to Jiande, proclaimed their intent to rebel, and Heita styled himself Grand General.

sentences.zh: 詔發關中步騎三千，使將軍秦武通、定州總管藍田李玄通擊之；

translations.literal: An edict dispatched three thousand infantry and cavalry from Guanzhong, ordering Generals Qin Wutong and Dingzhou Governor-General of Lantian Li Xuantong to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered three thousand foot and horse soldiers from Guanzhong sent out under General Qin Wutong and Li Xuantong of Lantian, governor-general of Dingzhou, to strike him down.

sentences.zh: 又詔幽州總管李藝引兵會擊黑闥。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered Li Yi, governor-general of Youzhou, to lead troops and join in attacking Heita.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered Li Yi, governor-general of Youzhou, to march and unite with the others in striking Heita down.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，突厥寇代州，總管李大恩遣行軍總管王孝基拒之，舉軍皆沒。

translations.literal: On guimao, the Turks raided Daizhou; Governor-General Li Da'en sent Campaigning Governor-General Wang Xiaoji to resist, and the entire army was wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day, Turks invaded Daizhou. Governor-general Li Da'en sent campaigning governor-general Wang Xiaoji to meet them, and the whole force was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，進圍崞縣。

translations.literal: On jiachen, they advanced to besiege Guo County.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day, the Turks pressed on to besiege Guo County.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，王孝基自突厥逃歸，李大恩眾少，據城自守，突厥不敢逼，月餘引去。

translations.literal: On yisi, Wang Xiaoji escaped from the Turks and returned; Li Da'en had few troops, held the city in defense, the Turks did not dare press the attack, and withdrew after more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day, Wang Xiaoji fled the Turks and got back. Li Da'en's force was too small to sally forth, so he held the city; the Turks did not dare close in and withdrew after a month and more.

sentences.zh: 上以南方寇盜尚多，丙午，以左武候將軍張鎮周為淮南道行軍總管，大將軍陳智略為嶺南道行軍總管，鎮撫之。

translations.literal: Because bandits and marauders were still numerous in the south, on bingwu the Emperor appointed Left Martial Guard General Zhang Zhenzhou Campaigning Governor-General of the Huainan Circuit and Grand General Chen Zhilve Campaigning Governor-General of the Lingnan Circuit to pacify the region.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits still ran riot in the south, so on the bingwu day the emperor named Left Martial Guard general Zhang Zhenzhou campaigning governor-general of Huainan and grand general Chen Zhilve campaigning governor-general of Lingnan to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 丁未，劉黑闥陷歷亭，執屯衛將軍王行敏，使之拜，不可，遂殺之。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Liu Heita captured Liting, seized Garrison Guard General Wang Xingmin, and ordered him to bow in submission; he refused, and Heita killed him.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day, Liu Heita took Liting, seized garrison guard general Wang Xingmin, and tried to make him bow; Wang refused, and Heita had him killed.

sentences.zh: 初，洛陽既平，徐圓朗請降，拜兗州總管，封魯郡公。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Luoyang had been pacified, Xu Yuanlang submitted and was appointed governor-general of Yanzhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Lu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang had first been pacified, Xu Yuanlang had surrendered; he was made governor-general of Yanzhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 劉黑闥作亂，陰與圓朗通謀。

translations.literal: When Liu Heita rose in rebellion, he secretly plotted with Yuanlang.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Heita rebelled, he and Yuanlang plotted together in secret.

sentences.zh: 上使葛公盛彥師安集河南，行至任城；

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Duke of Ge Sheng Yanshi to pacify and settle Henan; when he reached Rencheng,
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Duke of Ge Sheng Yanshi to pacify Henan; he had reached Rencheng when,

sentences.zh: 辛亥，圓朗執彥師，舉兵反。

translations.literal: on xinhai, Yuanlang seized Yanshi and raised troops in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: on the xinhai day, Yuanlang seized Yanshi and rose in arms.

sentences.zh: 黑闥以圓朗為大行臺元帥，兗、鄆、陳、杞、伊、洛、曹、戴等八州豪右皆應之。

translations.literal: Heita made Yuanlang Grand Marshal of the Grand Pacification Headquarters; the powerful gentry of eight prefectures—Yan, Yun, Chen, Qi, Yi, Luo, Cao, and Dai—all rallied to their cause.
translations.idiomatic: Heita appointed Yuanlang grand marshal of the grand pacification headquarters, and the great families of Yan, Yun, Chen, Qi, Yi, Luo, Cao, and Dai—eight prefectures in all—rallied to them.

sentences.zh: 圓朗厚禮彥師，使作書與其弟，令舉虞城降。

translations.literal: Yuanlang treated Yanshi with great courtesy and had him write a letter to his younger brother, ordering him to surrender Yucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlang honored Yanshi lavishly and made him write to his younger brother, telling him to surrender Yucheng.

sentences.zh: 彥師為書曰：「吾奉使無狀，為賊所擒，為臣不忠，誓之以死；

translations.literal: Yanshi wrote: "I disgraced my mission and was captured by rebels; as a minister I have been disloyal, and I swear to die for it;
translations.idiomatic: Yanshi wrote: "I failed shamefully in my commission and was taken by the rebels; I have been an unfaithful subject, and I swear to die for it;

sentences.zh: 汝善侍老母，勿以吾為念。

translations.literal: take good care of our old mother and do not grieve over me."
translations.idiomatic: serve our old mother well, and do not grieve for me."

sentences.zh: 」圓朗初色動，而彥師自若。

translations.literal: Yuanlang's expression changed at first, but Yanshi remained composed.
translations.idiomatic: At first Yuanlang's face changed color, but Yanshi was unmoved.

sentences.zh: 圓朗乃笑曰：「盛將軍有壯節，不可殺也。

translations.literal: Yuanlang then laughed and said, "General Sheng has a hero's steadfastness—it would be wrong to kill him."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlang then laughed and said, "General Sheng has the mettle of a hero; he must not be killed."

sentences.zh: 」待之如舊。

translations.literal: He treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: He treated Yanshi just as he had before.

sentences.zh: 河南道安撫大使任瑰行至宋州，屬圓朗反，副使柳浚勸瑰退保汴州，瑰笑曰：「柳以何怯也！

translations.literal: Ren Gui, commissioner for pacification of the Henan Circuit, reached Songzhou just as Yuanlang rebelled; Deputy Commissioner Liu Jun urged Gui to withdraw and hold Bianzhou. Gui laughed and said, "Why are you so fearful, Liu?"
translations.idiomatic: Ren Gui, commissioner for pacifying the Henan circuit, reached Songzhou just as Yuanlang rebelled. Deputy commissioner Liu Jun urged him to fall back and hold Bianzhou. Gui laughed: "Liu, why so timid?"

sentences.zh: 」圓朗又攻陷楚丘，引兵將圍虞城，瑰遣部將崔樞、張公謹自鄢陵帥諸州豪右質子百餘人守虞城。

translations.literal: Yuanlang also captured Chuqiu and marched to besiege Yucheng; Gui sent his subordinate generals Cui Shu and Zhang Gongjin from Yanling, leading more than a hundred hostages—the sons of the powerful gentry of various prefectures—to hold Yucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlang also took Chuqiu and marched to encircle Yucheng. Gui sent his officers Cui Shu and Zhang Gongjin from Yanling, at the head of more than a hundred hostages—the sons of the great families of several prefectures—to defend Yucheng.

sentences.zh: 濬曰：「樞與公謹皆王世充將，諸州質子父兄皆反，恐必為變。

translations.literal: Jun said, "Shu and Gongjin were both Wang Shichong's generals, and the hostages' fathers and elder brothers have all rebelled—they will surely turn against us."
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, "Shu and Gongjin both served Wang Shichong, and these hostages' fathers and elder brothers have all rebelled; they are sure to turn on us."

sentences.zh: 」瑰不應。

translations.literal: Gui did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Gui gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 樞至虞城，分質子使與土人合隊共守城。

translations.literal: When Shu reached Yucheng, he divided the hostages among the local militia units to defend the city together.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu reached Yucheng, he split the hostages among the local squads and had them defend the city together.

sentences.zh: 賊稍近，質子有叛者，樞斬其隊帥。

translations.literal: As the rebels drew near, some hostages defected; Shu executed their squad leader.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels closed in, some hostages tried to defect; Shu beheaded their squad leader.

sentences.zh: 於是諸隊帥皆懼，各殺其質子，樞不禁，梟其首於門外，遣使白瑰。

translations.literal: Thereupon all the squad leaders grew fearful and each killed his hostage; Shu did not stop them, had the heads displayed outside the gate, and sent a messenger to inform Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Then every squad leader, in fear, killed his hostage. Shu did not restrain them, had the heads hung outside the gate, and sent word to Gui.

sentences.zh: 瑰陽怒曰：「吾所以使與質子俱者，欲招其父兄耳，何罪而殺之！

translations.literal: Gui feigned anger and said, "The reason I sent them out with the hostages was to win over their fathers and elder brothers—what crime had they committed that you killed them!"
translations.idiomatic: Gui pretended to rage: "I sent them out with the hostages to win over their fathers and brothers—what crime had those boys committed, that you killed them!"

sentences.zh: 」退謂濬曰：「吾固知崔樞能辦此也。

translations.literal: In private he told Jun, "I knew all along that Cui Shu could handle this."
translations.idiomatic: In private he told Jun, "I always knew Cui Shu would see this through."

sentences.zh: 縣人既殺質子，與賊深仇，吾何患乎！

translations.literal: "Now that the townspeople have killed the hostages, they bear a deep hatred for the rebels—what have I to worry about!"
translations.idiomatic: "Now that the townsfolk have killed the hostages, they are the rebels' mortal enemies—what do I have to fear?"

sentences.zh: 」賊攻虞城，果不克而去。

translations.literal: The rebels attacked Yucheng but, as expected, failed to take it and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels assaulted Yucheng, failed to take it as expected, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 初，竇建德以鄱陽崔元遜為深州刺史，及劉黑闥反，元遜與其黨數十人謀於野，伏甲士於車中，以禾覆其上，詐為農人，直入聽事，自禾中呼噪而出，執刺史裴晞殺之，傳首黑闥。

translations.literal: Earlier, Dou Jiande had appointed Cui Yuansun of Poyang prefect of Shenzhou; when Liu Heita rebelled, Yuansun and several dozen of his followers plotted in the open country, hid armed men in carts, covered them with grain stalks, and disguised themselves as farmers; they went straight into the prefect's office, burst out shouting from beneath the grain, seized Prefect Pei Xi, killed him, and sent his head to Heita.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Dou Jiande had made the Poyang man Cui Yuansun prefect of Shenzhou. When Liu Heita rebelled, Yuansun and several dozen followers plotted in the fields, hid armed men in carts under sheaves of grain, and came disguised as farmers straight into the prefect's hall. They burst shouting from the grain, seized prefect Pei Xi, killed him, and sent his head to Heita.

sentences.zh: 九月，乙卯，文登賊帥-{淳于}-難請降；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on yimao, the bandit chief of Wendeng, Chunyu Nan, submitted in surrender;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the yimao day, the Wendeng bandit chief Chunyu Nan offered surrender;

sentences.zh: 置登州，以難為刺史。

translations.literal: Deng Prefecture was established, and Nan was made its prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Prefecture was established, and Nan was appointed its prefect.

sentences.zh: 突厥寇并州；

translations.literal: The Turks raided Bingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Turks raided Bingzhou;

sentences.zh: 遣左屯衛大將軍竇琮等擊之。

translations.literal: the Emperor sent Left Garrison Guard Grand General Dou Cong and others to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor dispatched left garrison guard grand general Dou Cong and others to drive them off.

sentences.zh: 戊午，突厥寇原州；

translations.literal: On wuwu, the Turks raided Yuanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day, Turks invaded Yuanzhou;

sentences.zh: 遣行軍總管尉遲敬德等擊之。

translations.literal: Campaigning Governor-General Yuchi Jingde and others were dispatched to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: campaigning governor-general Yuchi Jingde and others were sent to strike them.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，徐圓朗自稱魯王。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Xu Yuanlang styled himself King of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day, Xu Yuanlang proclaimed himself King of Lu.

sentences.zh: 隋末，歙州賊帥汪華據黟、歙等五州，有眾一萬，自稱吳王。

translations.literal: At the end of the Sui, the bandit chief of Shezhou, Wang Hua, held five prefectures including Yi and She, with ten thousand followers, and styled himself King of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui, the Shezhou bandit chief Wang Hua held Yi, She, and three other prefectures—ten thousand men in all—and styled himself King of Wu.

sentences.zh: 甲子，遣使來降；

translations.literal: On jiazi, he sent envoys to submit;
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day, he sent envoys to surrender;

sentences.zh: 拜歙州總管。

translations.literal: he was appointed governor-general of Shezhou.
translations.idiomatic: he was made governor-general of Shezhou.

sentences.zh: 隋末，弋陽盧祖尚糾合壯士以衛鄉里，部分嚴整，群盜畏之。

translations.literal: At the end of the Sui, Lu Zushang of Yiyang gathered stalwart men to defend his home district; his formations were strictly ordered, and the bandits feared him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui, Lu Zushang of Yiyang rallied stalwart men to guard his homeland. His ranks were tightly disciplined, and the bandits feared him.

sentences.zh: 及煬帝遇弒，鄉人奉之為光州刺史；

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang was assassinated, his fellow townsmen installed him as prefect of Guangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang was murdered, his neighbors installed him as prefect of Guangzhou;

sentences.zh: 時年十九，奉表於皇泰主。

translations.literal: he was then nineteen and submitted a memorial to the Prince of Huai of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: he was nineteen at the time and sent a memorial to the Prince of Huai of Tang.

sentences.zh: 及王世充自立，祖尚來降；

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong declared himself emperor, Zushang came over to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong seized the throne, Zushang came over in surrender;

sentences.zh: 丙子，以祖尚為光州總管。

translations.literal: on bingzi, Zushang was appointed governor-general of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: on the bingzi day, Zushang was made governor-general of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 己卯，詔括天下戶口。

translations.literal: On jimao, an edict ordered a census of households throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On the jimao day, an edict ordered a household census across the empire.

sentences.zh: 徐圓朗寇濟州，治中吳人及論擊走之。

translations.literal: Xu Yuanlang raided Jizhou; Administrative Assistant Wu Renji drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuanlang raided Jizhou; administrative assistant Wu Renji beat him back.

sentences.zh: 癸未，詔以太常樂工皆前代因罪配沒，子孫相承，多歷年所，良可哀愍；

translations.literal: On guiwei, an edict declared that the musicians of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices had all been assigned into servitude in earlier dynasties for crimes, and their descendants had inherited this status for many years—a matter truly deserving pity;
translations.idiomatic: On the guiwei day, an edict said that the Court of Imperial Sacrifices musicians had all been condemned to penal service in earlier ages for crimes, and their descendants had borne that burden for generations—truly a thing to pity;

sentences.zh: 宜並蠲除為民，且令執事，若仕宦入流，勿更追集。

translations.literal: they should all be released and restored to commoner status, and even those who had entered official ranks were not to be recalled for this service.
translations.idiomatic: all were to be released and made commoners, and even those who had entered office were not to be summoned back.

sentences.zh: 甲申，靈州總管楊師道擊突厥，破之。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Yang Shidao, governor-general of Lingzhou, attacked the Turks and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day, Yang Shidao, governor-general of Lingzhou, struck the Turks and routed them.

sentences.zh: 師道，恭仁之弟也。

translations.literal: Shidao was the younger brother of Gongren.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao was Gongren's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 詔發巴、蜀兵，以趙郡王孝恭為荊湘道行軍總管，李靖攝行軍長史，統十二總管，自夔州順流東下；

translations.literal: An edict mobilized troops from Ba and Shu, appointing Prince of Zhao Commandery Li Xiaogong Campaigning Governor-General of the Jingxiang Circuit, with Li Jing acting as campaigning chief of staff, commanding twelve governor-generals to descend eastward with the current from Kuizhou;
translations.idiomatic: An edict called up Ba and Shu troops, made Prince of Zhao Commandery Li Xiaogong campaigning governor-general of the Jingxiang circuit, and put Li Jing in charge as acting campaigning chief of staff, commanding twelve governor-generals to sail downriver from Kuizhou;

sentences.zh: 以廬江王瑗為荊郢道行軍元帥，出襄州道，黔州刺史田世康出辰州道，黃州總管周法明出夏口道，以擊蕭銑。

translations.literal: Prince of Lujiang Li Yuan was made Campaigning Marshal of the Jingying Circuit, advancing by the Xiangzhou route; Qianzhou Prefect Tian Shikang advanced by the Chenzhou route; Huangzhou Governor-General Zhou Faming advanced by the Xiakou route—all to strike Xiao Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Lujiang Li Yuan was made campaigning marshal of the Jingying circuit and marched by the Xiangzhou road; Qianzhou prefect Tian Shikang by the Chenzhou road; and Huangzhou governor-general Zhou Faming by the Xiakou road—to attack Xiao Xian.

sentences.zh: 是月，孝恭發夔州。

translations.literal: That month, Xiaogong set out from Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: That same month, Xiaogong departed from Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 時峽江方漲，諸將請俟水落進軍，李靖曰：「兵貴神速。

translations.literal: The gorge river was then in flood, and the generals asked to wait until the waters fell before advancing. Li Jing said, "In war, speed is precious.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangtze gorges were swollen, and the generals urged waiting for the flood to recede. Li Jing said, "Speed is the soul of war.

sentences.zh: 今吾兵始集，銑尚未知，若乘江漲，倏忽抵其城下，掩其不備，此必有擒；

translations.literal: Our forces have only just assembled, and Xian does not yet know; if we ride the rising river and suddenly reach his walls, catching him unprepared, he is sure to be taken;
translations.idiomatic: Our army has only just gathered, and Xian still does not know it. If we ride the flood and in a flash reach his city, striking before he is ready, we are bound to take him;

sentences.zh: 不可失也！

translations.literal: this chance must not be lost!"
translations.idiomatic: we must not let it slip away!"

sentences.zh: 」孝恭從之。

translations.literal: Xiaogong agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong followed his counsel.

sentences.zh: 淮安王神通將關內兵至冀州，與李藝兵合。

translations.literal: Prince of Huai'an Li Shentong led Guanzhong troops to Jizhou and joined Li Yi's force.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Huai'an Li Shentong brought Guanzhong troops to Jizhou and united with Li Yi's army.

sentences.zh: 又發邢、洺、相、魏、恆、趙等州兵合五萬餘人，與劉黑闥戰於饒陽城南，布陳十餘里；

translations.literal: Troops were also mobilized from Xing, Ming, Xiang, Wei, Heng, Zhao, and other prefectures, more than fifty thousand in all, to fight Liu Heita south of Raoyang; the battle line stretched more than ten li;
translations.idiomatic: Forces were also raised from Xing, Ming, Xiang, Wei, Heng, Zhao, and other prefectures—more than fifty thousand men—to meet Liu Heita south of Raoyang. The array stretched for more than ten li;

sentences.zh: 黑闥眾少，依堤單行而陳以當之。

translations.literal: Heita's force was smaller; he drew up in a single file along the embankment to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: Heita's numbers were fewer; he lined up in a single rank along the dike to hold them.

sentences.zh: 會風雪，神通乘風擊之，既而風返，神通大敗，士馬軍資失亡三分之二。

translations.literal: A windstorm came up; Shentong struck with the wind at his back, but then the wind shifted, and Shentong was routed; two-thirds of his men, horses, and supplies were lost.
translations.idiomatic: A snowstorm blew up. Shentong attacked with the wind at his back, but the wind turned, and he was crushed; two-thirds of his men, horses, and stores were lost.

sentences.zh: 李藝居西偏，擊高雅賢，破之，逐奔數里，聞大軍不利，退保蒿城；

translations.literal: Li Yi held the western wing, struck Gao Yaxian, defeated him, and pursued several li; hearing that the main army had failed, he withdrew to hold Gaocheng;
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi on the western flank struck Gao Yaxian, routed him, and chased him for several li; then, hearing the main force had failed, he fell back to hold Gaocheng;

sentences.zh: 黑闥就擊之，藝亦敗，薛萬均、萬徹皆為所虜，截發驅之。

translations.literal: Heita pressed the attack, and Yi was also defeated; Xue Wanjun and Wanche were both captured, their hair cut short, and they were driven before the enemy ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Heita pressed him there and Yi was beaten too. Xue Wanjun and Wanche were both taken captive, their hair shorn, and driven before the enemy.

sentences.zh: 萬均兄弟亡歸，藝引兵歸幽州。

translations.literal: The Xue brothers escaped and returned; Yi led his troops back to Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Xue brothers fled back; Yi withdrew to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 黑闥兵勢大振。

translations.literal: Heita's military power surged.
translations.idiomatic: Heita's momentum swelled greatly.

sentences.zh: 上以秦王世民功大，前代官皆不足以稱之，特置天策上將，位在王公上。

translations.literal: Because the Prince of Qin Shimin's achievements were so great that no title of earlier ages could do them justice, the Emperor specially created the post of Celestial Strategist General, ranking above kings and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin Shimin's feats were so great that no earlier rank could match them, so the emperor created a new office—Celestial Strategist General—above kings and dukes.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，以世民為天策上將，領司徒、陝東道大行臺尚書令，增邑二萬戶，仍開天策府，置官屬，以齊王元吉為司空。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, Shimin was made Celestial Strategist General, holding the posts of Minister over the Masses and Chief Minister of the Grand Pacification Headquarters of the Shandong Circuit, with his fief increased by twenty thousand households; he also opened the Celestial Strategist Office and appointed its staff, and Prince of Qi Yuanji was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, Shimin was named Celestial Strategist General, retaining Minister over the Masses and chief minister of the Shandong grand pacification headquarters, with his fief enlarged by twenty thousand households; he opened the Celestial Strategist Office with a full staff, and Prince of Qi Yuanji was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 世民以海內浸平，乃開館於宮西，延四方文學之士，出教以王府屬杜如晦、記室房玄齡、虞世南、文學褚亮、姚思廉、主簿李玄道、參軍蔡允恭、薛元敬、顏相時、咨議典簽蘇勖、天策府從事中郎於志宇、軍咨祭酒蘇世長、記室薛收、倉曹李守素、國子助教陸德明、孔穎達、信都蓋文達、宋州總管府戶曹許敬宗，並以本官兼文學館學士，分為三番，更日直宿，供給珍膳，恩禮優厚。

translations.literal: As the realm was gradually pacified, Shimin opened a hall west of the palace and invited men of letters from all quarters; by edict he named Prince's Household Attendant Du Ruhui, Secretariat Director Fang Xuanling, Yu Shinan, Literary Scholar Chu Liang, Yao Silian, Chief Clerk Li Xuandao, Staff Officers Cai Yungong, Xue Yuanjing, Yan Xiangshi, Advisory Clerk Su Xu, Celestial Strategist Office Attendant Yu Zhiyu, Military Adviser Su Shichang, Secretariat Director Xue Shou, Granary Officer Li Shousu, Erudites of the Imperial Academy Lu Deming, Kong Yingda, Xindu Gai Wenda, and Household Officer of the Songzhou Governor-General's Office Xu Jingzong—all retaining their original posts while also serving as scholars of the Literary Hall—divided into three watches to take turns on duty by day, with fine food provided and favor shown them in generous measure.
translations.idiomatic: With the empire nearly at peace, Shimin opened a hall west of the palace and gathered scholars from every quarter. By edict he named Du Ruhui, Fang Xuanling, Yu Shinan, Chu Liang, Yao Silian, Li Xuandao, Cai Yungong, Xue Yuanjing, Yan Xiangshi, Su Xu, Yu Zhiyu, Su Shichang, Xue Shou, Li Shousu, Lu Deming, Kong Yingda, Gai Wenda of Xindu, and Xu Jingzong—all to serve as Literary Hall scholars while keeping their original posts—split into three watches to stand duty in rotation, with rare fare and lavish honor.

sentences.zh: 世民朝謁公事之暇，輒至館中，引諸學士討論文籍，或夜分乃寢。

translations.literal: Whenever Shimin was free from court and official business, he would go to the hall, gather the scholars to discuss books, and sometimes did not sleep until midnight.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Shimin was free of court business, he went to the hall, drew the scholars into discussion of the classics, and sometimes slept only after midnight.

sentences.zh: 又使庫直閻立本圖像，褚亮為贊，號十八學士。

translations.literal: He also had the palace artist Yan Liben paint their portraits, with Chu Liang writing the inscriptions; they were called the Eighteen Scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He had palace artist Yan Liben paint their likenesses and Chu Liang write the captions; they were known as the Eighteen Scholars.

sentences.zh: 士大夫得預其選者，時人謂之「登瀛洲」。

translations.literal: Those among the gentry chosen for this company were said by contemporaries to have "ascended to the Isle of Immortals."
translations.idiomatic: Gentry chosen for this company were said by their contemporaries to have "ascended to the Isle of Immortals."

sentences.zh: 允恭，大寶之弟子；

translations.literal: Yungong was a disciple of Dabao;
translations.idiomatic: Yungong was a pupil of Dabao;

sentences.zh: 元敬，收之從子；

translations.literal: Yuanjing was Shou's nephew;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing was Shou's nephew;

sentences.zh: 相時，師古之弟；

translations.literal: Xiangshi was Shigu's younger brother;
translations.idiomatic: Xiangshi was Shigu's younger brother;

sentences.zh: 立本，毘之子也。

translations.literal: Liben was Pi's son.
translations.idiomatic: Liben was Pi's son.

sentences.zh: 初，杜如晦為秦王府兵曹參軍，俄遷陝州長史。

translations.literal: Earlier, Du Ruhui had been a Military Staff Officer of the Prince of Qin's household and was soon transferred to be chief administrator of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Du Ruhui had served as a military staff officer in the Prince of Qin's household and was soon posted as chief administrator of Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時府僚多補外官，世民患之。

translations.literal: At the time many household staff were being assigned to outside posts, and Shimin was troubled by it.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the prince's staff were being sent to outside posts, and Shimin was troubled.

sentences.zh: 房玄齡曰：「餘人不足惜，至於杜如晦，王佐之才，大王欲經營四方，非如晦不可。

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling said, "The others are not worth regretting, but as for Du Ruhui, he has the talent of a king's assistant; if Your Highness means to secure the realm, you cannot do without Ruhui."
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling said, "The rest are no great loss, but Du Ruhui has the talent of a king's right hand. If you mean to win the realm, you cannot do without him."

sentences.zh: 」世民驚曰：「微公言，幾失之。

translations.literal: Shimin started and said, "But for your words, I would nearly have lost him."
translations.idiomatic: Shimin started and said, "Had you not spoken, I would almost have lost him."

sentences.zh: 」即奏為府屬。

translations.literal: He immediately memorialized to have Ruhui made a household attache.
translations.idiomatic: He at once memorialized to have Ruhui made a household attache.

sentences.zh: 與玄齡常從世民征伐，參謀帷幄，軍中多事，如晦剖決如流。

translations.literal: Together with Xuanling he often followed Shimin on campaign, advising within the command tent; though the army was beset with affairs, Ruhui's decisions flowed like water.
translations.idiomatic: With Xuanling he often followed Shimin to war, counseling in the command tent; though the camp was awash in business, Ruhui's judgments ran clear as a stream.

sentences.zh: 世民每破軍克城，諸將佐爭取寶貨，玄齡獨收采人物，致之幕府。

translations.literal: Whenever Shimin broke an enemy army or took a city, the generals and staff scrambled for treasure; Xuanling alone gathered men of talent and brought them to the prince's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Shimin routed a foe or took a city, his officers fought over loot; Xuanling alone gathered men of ability and sent them to the prince's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 又將佐有勇略者，玄齡必與之深相結，使為世民盡死力。

translations.literal: When any officer had courage and strategy, Xuanling always bound himself closely to him, so that he would give Shimin his utmost loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an officer showed courage and wit, Xuanling bound himself to him, so that the man would give Shimin his life.

sentences.zh: 世民每令玄齡入奏事，上歎曰：「玄齡為吾兒陳事，雖隔千里，皆如面談。

translations.literal: Whenever Shimin sent Xuanling in to report, the Emperor sighed and said, "Xuanling presents my son's business; though a thousand li apart, it is as though they spoke face to face."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Shimin sent Xuanling in to report, the emperor sighed: "Xuanling lays out my son's affairs; though a thousand li divide them, it is as if they spoke face to face."

sentences.zh: 」李玄道嘗事李密，為記室，密敗，官屬為王世充所虜，懼死，皆達曙不寐。

translations.literal: Li Xuandao had once served Li Mi as secretariat director; when Mi was defeated, the staff were captured by Wang Shichong; fearing death, they all stayed awake until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuandao had once served Li Mi as secretariat director. When Mi fell, the staff were taken by Wang Shichong; fearing death, they all kept vigil till dawn.

sentences.zh: 獨玄道起居自若，曰：「死生有命，非憂可免！

translations.literal: Xuandao alone went about as usual and said, "Life and death are fated—worry cannot avert them!"
translations.idiomatic: Xuandao alone kept his composure and said, "Life and death are ordained—worry cannot ward them off!"

sentences.zh: 」眾服其識量。

translations.literal: The others admired his breadth of mind.
translations.idiomatic: The rest admired his calm judgment.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，劉黑闥陷瀛州，殺刺史盧士睿。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Liu Heita captured Yingzhou and killed Prefect Lu Shirui.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day, Liu Heita took Yingzhou and killed prefect Lu Shirui.

sentences.zh: 觀州人執刺史雷德備，以城降之。

translations.literal: The people of Guan Prefecture seized Prefect Lei Debei and surrendered the city to him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Guan Prefecture seized prefect Lei Debei and surrendered the city to him.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，蕭銑鄂州刺史雷長穎以魯山來降。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Lei Changying, prefect of Ezhou under Xiao Xian, surrendered Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao day, Lei Changying, Xiao Xian's prefect of Ezhou, surrendered Lushan.

sentences.zh: 趙郡王孝恭帥戰艦二千餘艘東下，蕭銑以江水方漲，殊不為備；

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Commandery Li Xiaogong led more than two thousand warships eastward; Xiao Xian, thinking the river was still in flood, made no special preparations;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhao Commandery Li Xiaogong sailed east with more than two thousand warships. Xiao Xian, thinking the river still in flood, was wholly unprepared;

sentences.zh: 孝恭等拔其荊門、宜都二鎮，進至夷陵。

translations.literal: Xiaogong and the others took his garrisons at Jingmen and Yidu and advanced to Yiling.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong's force took the Jingmen and Yidu garrisons and pushed on to Yiling.

sentences.zh: 銑將文士弘將精兵數萬屯清江，癸巳，孝恭擊走之，獲戰艦三百餘艘，殺溺死者萬計；

translations.literal: Xian's general Wen Shihong encamped at Qingjiang with tens of thousands of picked troops; on guisi, Xiaogong routed him, capturing more than three hundred warships; those killed or drowned numbered in the tens of thousands;
translations.idiomatic: Xian's general Wen Shihong held Qingjiang with tens of thousands of elite troops. On the guisi day, Xiaogong drove him off, seizing more than three hundred warships; those killed or drowned ran to the tens of thousands;

sentences.zh: 追奔至百里洲，士弘收兵復戰，又敗之，進入北江。

translations.literal: the pursuit reached Baili Isle; Shihong regrouped and fought again, was defeated again, and they entered the northern Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: the pursuit reached Baili Isle. Shihong rallied and fought again, was beaten again, and they entered the northern Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 銑江州總管蓋彥舉以五州來降。

translations.literal: Xian's Jiangzhou Governor-General Gai Yanshu surrendered five prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's Jiangzhou governor-general Gai Yanshu surrendered five prefectures.

sentences.zh: 毛州刺史趙元愷，性嚴急，下不堪命。

translations.literal: Zhao Yuankai, prefect of Maozhou, was harsh and severe by nature, and his subordinates could not endure it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yuankai, prefect of Maozhou, was by nature harsh and severe, and those beneath him could not bear it.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，州民董燈明等作亂，殺元愷以應劉黑闥。

translations.literal: On dingmao, the prefectural people Dong Dengming and others rose in revolt, killed Yuankai, and joined Liu Heita.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao day, the townsman Dong Dengming and others rebelled, killed Yuankai, and rallied to Liu Heita.

sentences.zh: 盛彥師自徐圓朗所逃歸。

translations.literal: Sheng Yanshi escaped from Xu Yuanlang's camp and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yanshi fled Xu Yuanlang's camp and got back.

sentences.zh: 王薄因說青、萊、密諸州，皆下之。

translations.literal: Wang Bo went on to persuade Qing, Lai, and Mi prefectures, and all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bo then won over Qing, Lai, and Mi prefectures, and all came over.

sentences.zh: 蕭銑之罷兵營農也，才留宿衛數千人，聞唐兵至，文士弘敗，大懼，倉猝徵兵，皆在江、嶺之外，道塗阻遠，不能遽集，乃悉見兵出拒戰。

translations.literal: When Xiao Xian had disbanded his troops to farm the land, he had left only a few thousand guards; hearing that Tang troops had arrived and that Wen Shihong had been defeated, he was greatly afraid; he hastily called up troops, but they were all beyond the river and the mountain ranges, the roads long and hard, and could not be gathered quickly; so he sent out every soldier he had to meet the attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Xian had stood his army down to farm, he had kept only a few thousand guards. Learning that Tang forces had come and that Wen Shihong was beaten, he was terrified. He tried to raise troops in haste, but they were all beyond the rivers and southern ranges, the roads long and hard, and could not be gathered quickly; so he sent every man he had to meet the Tang army.

sentences.zh: 孝恭將擊之，李靖止之曰：「彼救敗之師，策非素立，勢不能久，不若且泊南岸，緩之一日，彼必分其兵，或留拒我，或歸自守；

translations.literal: Xiaogong was about to attack. Li Jing stopped him and said, "They are rescuing a defeated army; their plans were not long laid, and the position cannot hold. Better to anchor on the south bank and give them a day's respite—they will surely divide their forces, some staying to block us, some returning to defend on their own;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong was ready to strike when Li Jing stayed his hand. "They are rushing to save a broken army," he said. "Their strategy was never settled; they cannot hold long. Better to moor on the south bank and let a day pass—they will split their forces, some to hold us off, some to hurry home and defend;

sentences.zh: 兵分勢弱，我乘其懈而擊之，蔑不勝矣。

translations.literal: once their forces are divided their strength is weakened; we strike when they slacken, and we cannot fail to win.
translations.idiomatic: divide them and they weaken; catch them unguarded and we cannot fail to win.

sentences.zh: 今若急之，彼則並力死戰，楚兵剽銳，未易當也。

translations.literal: If we press them now, they will unite and fight to the death. Chu troops are fierce and sharp—not easily matched.
translations.idiomatic: Press them now and they will mass and die fighting. Chu soldiers are swift and keen—not easily faced.

sentences.zh: 」孝恭不從，留靖守營，自帥銳師出戰，果敗走，趣南岸。

translations.literal: " Xiaogong would not listen. He left Jing to guard the camp and personally led crack troops into battle; he was indeed defeated and fled, making for the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaogong refused. He left Jing to hold the camp, took the elite force out himself—and was beaten back, fleeing toward the south bank.

sentences.zh: 銑眾委舟收掠軍資，人皆負重，靖見其眾亂，縱兵奮擊，大破之，乘勝直抵江陵，入其外郭。

translations.literal: Xiao's men abandoned their boats to gather and plunder military supplies; everyone was laden. Jing saw their forces in disorder and unleashed his troops in fierce attack, routing them utterly; riding the victory he pressed straight to Jiangling and entered its outer city.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao's troops left their boats to loot supplies until every man staggered under the weight. Jing saw the disorder, loosed his men in a furious charge, and broke them completely; pressing the victory he drove straight to Jiangling and entered the outer wall.

sentences.zh: 又攻水城，拔之，大獲舟艦，李靖使孝恭盡散之江中。

translations.literal: He then attacked the water fort, took it, and captured a great haul of boats and ships. Li Jing had Xiaogong scatter them all on the river.
translations.idiomatic: He next stormed the water fort, took it, and seized a vast fleet. Li Jing ordered Xiaogong to cast every vessel adrift on the river.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆曰：「破敵所獲，當藉其用，奈何棄以資敵？

translations.literal: The generals all said, "What we gained by defeating the enemy ought to serve our use—why cast it away to aid the foe?
translations.idiomatic: The generals protested: "Spoils taken in victory ought to serve us—why throw them away and arm the enemy?"

sentences.zh: 」靖曰：「蕭銑之地，南出嶺表，東距洞庭。

translations.literal: " Jing said, "Xiao Xuan's territory extends south through the Ling region and east borders on Dongting.
translations.idiomatic: " Jing answered, "Xiao Xuan's domain runs south into Lingnan and east to Dongting Lake.

sentences.zh: 吾懸軍深入，若攻城未拔，援兵四集，吾表裡受敵，進退不獲，雖有舟楫，將安用之？

translations.literal: We have marched deep with isolated forces. If we fail to take the city at once and relief troops gather from all sides, we will be struck from within and without, unable to advance or retreat—though we have boats and ships, what use would they be?
translations.idiomatic: We are deep in hostile country with our line cut. Fail to storm the city quickly and relief will converge from every quarter—we will be caught inside and out, with nowhere to go. What good would a fleet do us then?

sentences.zh: 今棄舟艦，使塞江而下，援兵見之，必謂江陵已破，未敢輕進，往來覘伺，動淹旬月，吾取之必矣。

translations.literal: Now, if we discard the boats and ships and let them choke the river drifting downstream, the relief troops will see them and surely think Jiangling has fallen—they will not dare advance lightly, but go back and forth spying, often delaying ten days or a month; then we will take it for certain.
translations.idiomatic: Cast the ships adrift to clog the river downstream. When relief sees them they will assume Jiangling has fallen, dare not push forward, and spend weeks circling and spying—we will have the city for certain."

sentences.zh: 」銑援兵見舟艦，果疑不進。

translations.literal: " Xiao's relief troops saw the boats and ships and indeed hesitated and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiao's reinforcements sighted the drifting fleet and, as Jing had foreseen, hung back.

sentences.zh: 其交州總管丘和、長史高士廉、司馬杜之松等將朝江陵，聞銑敗，悉詣孝恭降。

translations.literal: Jiaozhou governor-general Qiu He, chief administrator Gao Shilian, vice chief administrator Du Zhisong, and others were on their way to attend court at Jiangling; hearing Xiao was defeated, they all went to Xiaogong and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhou governor-general Qiu He, chief administrator Gao Shilian, vice administrator Du Zhisong, and others were en route to Jiangling to pay court. When they heard Xiao was broken, they all came to Xiaogong and submitted.

sentences.zh: 孝恭勒兵圍江陵，銑內外阻絕，問策於中書侍郎岑文本，文本勸銑降。

translations.literal: Xiaogong drew up his troops and besieged Jiangling. Xiao was cut off within and without. He sought counsel from Secretariat Vice Director Cen Wenben; Wenben urged Xiao to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong tightened the siege around Jiangling until Xiao was sealed off inside and out. He asked Secretariat Vice Director Cen Wenben for counsel; Wenben urged surrender.

sentences.zh: 銑乃謂群下曰：「天不祚梁，不可復支矣。

translations.literal: Xiao then said to his followers, "Heaven does not bless Liang—it can no longer be upheld.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao told his court, "Heaven has abandoned Liang. We cannot stand any longer.

sentences.zh: 若必待力屈，則百姓蒙患，奈何以我一人之故，陷百姓於塗炭乎！

translations.literal: If we must wait until our strength is exhausted, the common people will suffer calamity—how can I for my sake alone plunge the people into fire and ruin!
translations.idiomatic: If we wait until we are broken, the people will pay the price—how can I, for one man's sake, drag them through fire and ash!"

sentences.zh: 」乙巳，銑以太牢告於太廟，下令開門出降，守城者皆哭。

translations.literal: " On yisi, Xiao announced with the grand sacrificial offering at the ancestral temple, ordered the gates opened and surrendered; those defending the city all wept.
translations.idiomatic: " On yisi he offered the grand sacrifice at the ancestral temple, opened the gates, and surrendered. The defenders wept.

sentences.zh: 銑帥群臣緦縗布幘詣軍門，曰：「當死者唯銑耳，百姓無罪，願不殺掠。

translations.literal: Xiao led his ministers, wearing hemp mourning dress and cloth headbands, to the army gate and said, "Only Xiao deserves death; the people are innocent. I beg that you not kill and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao came to the gate in hemp mourning and a cloth headcloth, his ministers behind him. "Let only Xiao die," he said. "The people are guiltless. Spare them looting and slaughter."

sentences.zh: 」孝恭入據其城，諸將欲大掠，岑文本說孝恭曰：「江南之民，自隋末以來，困於虐政，重以群雄虎爭，今之存者，皆鋒鏑之餘，跂踵延頸以望真主，是以蕭氏君臣、江陵父老決計歸命，庶幾有所息肩。

translations.literal: " Xiaogong entered and occupied the city. The generals wished to plunder on a great scale. Cen Wenben persuaded Xiaogong, saying, "The people of Jiangnan, since the end of Sui, have been worn down by tyrannical government, and further by warring warlords contending like tigers. Those who survive now are what remains after blades and arrows; they stand on tiptoe and stretch their necks awaiting a true sovereign. That is why the Xiao court and Jiangling's elders resolved to submit, hoping at last for a moment's rest.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaogong took the city. The generals wanted a general sack. Cen Wenben pleaded with him: "Since the fall of Sui, Jiangnan has groaned under cruelty and the tiger-fights of rival warlords. Those still alive are survivors of blade and arrow—they crane their necks toward a true lord. That is why the Xiao court and Jiangling's elders chose surrender, hoping at last to breathe."

sentences.zh: 今若縱兵俘掠，使士民失望，恐自此以南，無復向化之心矣！

translations.literal: If we now let the troops loose to capture and loot, making officials and people lose hope, I fear that from here southward there will never again be hearts inclined toward submission!
translations.idiomatic: Unleash the soldiers now and you crush that hope. I fear nothing south of here will ever turn toward us again!"

sentences.zh: 」孝恭稱善，遽禁止之。

translations.literal: " Xiaogong praised the advice and immediately forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaogong agreed and stopped the looting at once.

sentences.zh: 諸將又言：「梁之將帥與官軍拒斗死者，其罪既深，請籍沒其家，以賞將士。

translations.literal: The generals spoke again: "The Liang commanders who died fighting our official army—their crime is grave. We ask that their households be confiscated and registered to reward the officers and men.
translations.idiomatic: The generals pressed again: "Liang officers who fell fighting our army have sinned deeply. Confiscate their estates to reward the troops."

sentences.zh: 」李靖曰：「王者之師，宜使義聲先路。

translations.literal: " Li Jing said, "The army of a true king ought to let the voice of righteousness go first.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Jing said, "An army of kings should let righteousness march ahead of it.

sentences.zh: 彼為其主斗死，乃忠臣也，豈可同叛逆之科籍其家乎！

translations.literal: They died fighting for their lord—they are loyal ministers. How can we treat them like rebels and confiscate their households!
translations.idiomatic: They died for their master—they are loyal men. Would you punish them as rebels and strip their families!"

sentences.zh: 」於是城中安堵，秋毫無犯。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the city was settled and undisturbed; not the slightest thing was violated.
translations.idiomatic: " The city grew calm; not a hair was touched.

sentences.zh: 南方州縣聞之，皆望風款附。

translations.literal: Southern prefectures and counties heard of it and all came over at the first wind of submission.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties across the south heard and submitted at the first rumor of Tang justice.

sentences.zh: 銑降數日，援兵至者十餘萬，聞江陵不守，皆釋甲而降。

translations.literal: A few days after Xiao surrendered, relief troops arrived—more than a hundred thousand. Hearing Jiangling had fallen, they all cast off armor and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Within days of Xiao's surrender, more than a hundred thousand reinforcements arrived. Learning Jiangling was lost, they laid down arms and submitted.

sentences.zh: 孝恭送銑於長安，上數之。

translations.literal: Xiaogong sent Xiao to Chang'an. The Emperor reprimanded him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong escorted Xiao to Chang'an. The emperor rebuked him to his face.

sentences.zh: 銑曰：「隋失其鹿，天下共逐之。

translations.literal: Xiao said, "When Sui lost the stag, all under heaven joined in the chase.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao replied, "When Sui lost the deer, the realm ran after it.

sentences.zh: 銑無天命，故至此；

translations.literal: Xiao lacked Heaven's mandate, hence I have come to this;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao had no mandate from Heaven, and so I stand here;

sentences.zh: 若以為罪，無所逃死！

translations.literal: if you call it crime, there is no escaping death!
translations.idiomatic: call it crime and death is all that remains!"

sentences.zh: 」竟斬於都市。

translations.literal: " In the end he was executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: " He was beheaded in the public square.

sentences.zh: 詔以孝恭為荊州總管；

translations.literal: An edict made Xiaogong governor-general of Jingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Xiaogong governor-general of Jingzhou;

sentences.zh: 李靖為上柱國，賜爵永康縣公，仍使之安撫嶺南，得承制拜授。

translations.literal: Li Jing was made Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Yongkang County, and still sent to pacify Lingnan, with authority to appoint and confer by imperial commission.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing was made Pillar of State and Duke of Yongkang County, then sent to pacify Lingnan with full authority to appoint and enfeoff by imperial commission.

sentences.zh: 先是，銑遣黃門侍郎江陵劉洎略地嶺表，得五十餘城，未還而銑敗，洎以所得城來降；

translations.literal: Earlier, Xiao had sent Huangmen Vice Director Liu Ji of Jiangling to seize territory in Lingnan and had taken more than fifty cities. Before he returned, Xiao was defeated; Ji came in surrender with the cities he had taken;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xiao had dispatched Huangmen Vice Director Liu Ji of Jiangling to conquer Lingnan; Ji had taken more than fifty cities. Before he could return, Xiao fell—Ji came in with his conquests and submitted;

sentences.zh: 除南康州都督府長史。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief administrator of the Nankang Governor-General's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief administrator of the Nankang governor-general's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 戊申，徐圓朗昌州治中劉善行以須昌來降。

translations.literal: On wushen, Liu Shanxing, assistant prefect of Changzhou under Xu Yuanlang, surrendered with Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Liu Shanxing, assistant prefect of Changzhou under Xu Yuanlang, surrendered Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，詔陝東道大行臺尚書省自令、僕至郎中、主事，品秩皆與京師同，而員數差少，山東行臺及總管府、諸州並隸焉。

translations.literal: On gengxu, an edict declared that for the Eastern Shaan Grand Traveling Platform's Secretariat, from the chief and vice directors down to bureau heads and clerks, ranks and grades were all the same as in the capital, though the number of posts was somewhat fewer; the Shandong traveling platform and governor-general headquarters and all prefectures were placed under its authority.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu an edict fixed the Eastern Shaan grand traveling platform's secretariat—from chief and vice directors down to bureau heads and clerks—at the same ranks as the capital, though with fewer posts; the Shandong traveling platform, all governor-general headquarters, and every prefecture were placed under it.

sentences.zh: 其益州、襄州、山東、淮南、河北等道令、僕以下，各降京師一等，員數又減焉。

translations.literal: For the chiefs and vice directors and below in the circuits of Yizhou, Xiangzhou, Shandong, Huainan, Hebei, and others, each was reduced one grade below the capital, and the number of posts was further reduced.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yizhou, Xiangzhou, Shandong, Huainan, Hebei, and other circuits, ranks from chief and vice director downward were each lowered one grade below the capital, with still fewer posts.

sentences.zh: 行臺尚書令得承制補署。

translations.literal: The traveling platform chief of the secretariat was empowered to appoint and fill posts by imperial commission.
translations.idiomatic: The traveling platform secretariat chief was authorized to appoint officials by imperial commission.

sentences.zh: 其秦王、齊王府官之外，各置左右六護軍府，及左右親事帳內府。

translations.literal: Besides the officials of the Prince of Qin and Prince of Qi's households, there were established Left and Right Six Guard Offices, and Left and Right Personal Attendant Inner Household Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the Prince of Qin and Prince of Qi's household staffs, left and right Six Guard Offices were established, together with left and right Personal Attendant Inner Household Offices.

sentences.zh: 閏月，乙卯，上幸稷州；

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on yimao, the Emperor visited Jizhou;
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on yimao, the emperor visited Jizhou;

sentences.zh: 己未，幸武功舊墅；

translations.literal: on jiwei, he visited his old villa at Wugong;
translations.idiomatic: on jiwei, his old villa at Wugong;

sentences.zh: 壬戌，獵於好畤；

translations.literal: on renxu, he hunted at Haochi;
translations.idiomatic: on renxu, he hunted at Haochi;

sentences.zh: 乙丑，獵於九嵕；

translations.literal: on yichou, he hunted at Jiuyu;
translations.idiomatic: on yichou, at Jiuyu;

sentences.zh: 丁卯，獵於仲山；

translations.literal: on dingmao, he hunted at Zhongshan;
translations.idiomatic: on dingmao, at Zhongshan;

sentences.zh: 戊辰，獵於清水谷，遂幸三原；

translations.literal: on wuchen, he hunted at Qingshui Valley, then visited Sanyuan;
translations.idiomatic: on wuchen, at Qingshui Valley, then on to Sanyuan;

sentences.zh: 辛未，幸周氏陂；

translations.literal: on xinwei, he visited the Zhou clan embankment;
translations.idiomatic: on xinwei, the Zhou clan embankment;

sentences.zh: 壬申，還長安。

translations.literal: on renshen, he returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: on renshen, he returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲申，上祀圜丘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jiashen, the Emperor sacrificed at the Round Altar.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jiashen, the emperor offered sacrifice at the Round Altar to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 杜伏威使其將王雄誕擊李子通，子通以精兵守獨松嶺。

translations.literal: Du Fuwei sent his general Wang Xiongdan to attack Li Zitong; Zitong held Dusong Ridge with elite troops.
translations.idiomatic: Du Fuwei sent his general Wang Xiongdan against Li Zitong, who barred Dusong Ridge with picked troops.

sentences.zh: 雄誕遣其裨將陳當將千餘人，乘高據險以逼之，多張旗幟，夜則縛炬火於樹，佈滿山澤。

translations.literal: Xiongdan sent his lieutenant Chen Dang with more than a thousand men to seize the heights and hold the passes, pressing close; they spread many banners, and by night bound torches to trees until the hills and marshes blazed with light.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongdan dispatched his lieutenant Chen Dang with a thousand-odd men to take the high ground and choke the passes, pressing in close. They raised banner after banner; by night they lashed torches to the trees until hill and marsh glowed.

sentences.zh: 子通懼，燒營走保杭州；

translations.literal: Zitong was afraid, burned his camp, and fled to hold Hangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Zitong panicked, burned his camp, and fled to Hangzhou;

sentences.zh: 雄誕追擊之，又敗之於城下。

translations.literal: Xiongdan pursued and defeated him again below the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongdan chased him down and routed him again beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，子通窮蹙請降。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Zitong, driven to desperation, asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, cornered, Zitong sued for surrender.

sentences.zh: 伏威執子通並其左僕射樂伯通送長安；

translations.literal: Fuwei seized Zitong and his Left Vice Director Yue Botong and sent them to Chang'an;
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei took Zitong and his Left Vice Director Yue Botong in custody and sent them to Chang'an;

sentences.zh: 上釋之。

translations.literal: The Emperor released them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor set them free.

sentences.zh: 先是，汪華據黟、歙，稱王十餘年。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Hua had held Yi and She, styling himself king for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Hua had held Yi and She and styled himself king for more than a decade.

sentences.zh: 雄誕還軍擊之，華拒之於新安洞口，甲兵甚銳。

translations.literal: Xiongdan turned his army back to strike him. Hua blocked him at the Xinan cave mouth with very sharp armored troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongdan wheeled his army about to strike him. Hua barred the Xinan cave mouth with armored troops in hard fighting trim.

sentences.zh: 雄誕伏精兵於山谷，帥羸弱數千犯其陳，戰才合，陽不勝，走還營；

translations.literal: Xiongdan hid elite troops in the valleys, led several thousand weak troops to strike Hua's formation; when battle was barely joined he feigned defeat and fled back to camp;
translations.idiomatic: Xiongdan hid crack troops in the valleys, then led a few thousand weak men against Hua's line. Hardly had the clash begun when he feigned defeat and ran back to camp;

sentences.zh: 華進攻之，不能克，會日暮，引還，伏兵已據其洞口，華不得入，窘迫請降。

translations.literal: Hua pressed the attack but could not overcome them. At dusk he withdrew; the ambush had already seized his cave mouth—Hua could not enter, and in straits he asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Hua pressed the attack but could not break them. At dusk he pulled back—and found the ambush already holding his cave mouth. Shut out and trapped, he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 聞人遂安據昆山，無民屬，伏威使雄誕擊之。

translations.literal: Wenren Sui'an held Kunshan with no subjects beneath him. Fuwei sent Xiongdan to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Wenren Sui'an held Kunshan with no people under him. Fuwei sent Xiongdan against him.

sentences.zh: 雄誕以昆山險隘，難以力勝，乃單騎造其城下，陳國威靈，示以禍福。

translations.literal: Xiongdan thought Kunshan steep and narrow, hard to overcome by force; so he rode alone to the foot of the city, set forth the state's majesty, and showed fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Kunshan was steep and tight—force alone would not take it. Xiongdan rode in alone to the foot of the walls, spoke of the empire's might, and laid out blessing and ruin.

sentences.zh: 遂安感悅，帥諸將出降。

translations.literal: Sui'an was moved and pleased; he led his generals out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Sui'an was won over and led his officers out to submit.

sentences.zh: 於是伏威盡有淮南、江東之地，南至嶺，東距海。

translations.literal: Thereupon Fuwei held all the territory of Huainan and Jiangdong—south to the ranges, east to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei now held all Huainan and Jiangdong—south to the mountain ranges, east to the sea.

sentences.zh: 雄誕以功除歙州總管，賜爵宜春郡公。

translations.literal: For his merit Xiongdan was appointed governor-general of Shezhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Yichun Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For his service Xiongdan was made governor-general of Shezhou and enfeoffed Duke of Yichun Commandery.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，林州總管劉旻擊劉屳成，大破之。

translations.literal: On renchen, Linzhou governor-general Liu Min attacked Liu Xiancheng and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Linzhou governor-general Liu Min struck Liu Xiancheng and broke him completely.
