sentences.zh: 屳成僅以身免，部落皆降。

translations.literal: Xiancheng escaped with his life alone; all the tribes submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng alone escaped with his life; every tribe came over.

sentences.zh: 李靖度嶺，遣使分道招撫諸州，所至皆下。

translations.literal: Li Jing crossed the ranges, sent messengers by separate routes to win over and pacify the prefectures—all fell where they went.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing crossed the ranges and sent envoys by separate roads to win the prefectures over. Wherever they went, cities submitted.

sentences.zh: 蕭銑桂州總管李襲志帥所部諸州來降，趙郡王孝恭即以襲志為桂州總管，明年入朝。

translations.literal: Xiao Xuan's Guizhou governor-general Li Xizhi led the prefectures under his command to surrender; Prince of Zhao Commandery Li Xiaogong immediately made Xizhi governor-general of Guizhou; the next year he came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xizhi, Xiao Xuan's Guizhou governor-general, brought the prefectures under him to surrender. Prince of Zhao Commandery Li Xiaogong at once made him Guizhou governor-general; the next year he came to court.

sentences.zh: 以李靖為嶺南撫慰大使，檢校桂州總管，引兵下九十六州，得戶六十餘萬。

translations.literal: Li Jing was made Pacification Commissioner of Lingnan and acting governor-general of Guizhou; he led troops to subdue ninety-six prefectures and gained more than six hundred thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing was named Pacification Commissioner of Lingnan and acting Guizhou governor-general. He marched through ninety-six prefectures and registered more than six hundred thousand households.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，劉黑闥陷定州，執總管李玄通，黑闥愛其才，欲以為大將，玄通不可。

translations.literal: On renyin, Liu Heita took Dingzhou and seized governor-general Li Xuantong. Heita admired his talent and wished to make him a great general; Xuantong refused.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Liu Heita took Dingzhou and captured governor-general Li Xuantong. Heita admired his ability and wanted him for a chief commander; Xuantong would not yield.

sentences.zh: 故吏有以酒肉饋之者，玄通曰：「諸君哀吾幽辱，幸以酒肉來相開慰，當為諸君一醉。

translations.literal: Former subordinates brought him wine and meat. Xuantong said, "You pity my imprisonment and disgrace, and kindly bring wine and meat to comfort me—I ought to drink with you till we are drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Former aides brought him wine and meat. Xuantong said, "You pity my shame in captivity and bring wine and meat to comfort me—I ought to drink you under the table.

sentences.zh: 」酒酣，謂守者曰：「吾能劍舞，願假吾刀。

translations.literal: " When the wine was deep he said to his guards, "I can perform sword-dance—lend me a blade.
translations.idiomatic: " When he was drunk he told his guards, "I can dance with a sword—lend me a blade.

sentences.zh: 」守者與之，玄通舞竟，太息曰：「大丈夫受國厚恩，鎮撫方面，不能保全所守，亦何面目視息世間哉！

translations.literal: " The guards gave him one. When Xuantong finished the dance he sighed deeply and said, "A great man who has received thick grace from the state and governed a frontier—unable to hold what he was charged to hold—what face has he to draw breath in this world!
translations.idiomatic: " They gave him one. When the dance was done he sighed: "A man who has eaten the state's bounty and held a frontier—unable to keep what he was charged to keep—what face has he left to live?"

sentences.zh: 」即引刀自刺，潰腹而死。

translations.literal: " He immediately turned the blade on himself, ripped open his belly, and died.
translations.idiomatic: " He turned the blade on himself, ripped open his belly, and died.

sentences.zh: 上聞，為之流涕，拜其子伏護為大將。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard, he wept for him and appointed his son Fuhu a great general.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he wept and made his son Fuhu a great general.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，杞人周文舉殺刺史王文矩，以城應徐圓朗。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Zhou Wenju of Qi Prefecture killed prefect Wang Wenju and surrendered the city to Xu Yuanlang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Zhou Wenju of Qi Prefecture killed prefect Wang Wenju and handed the city to Xu Yuanlang.

sentences.zh: 幽州大饑，高開道許以粟賑之。

translations.literal: Youzhou suffered great famine. Gao Kaidao promised grain to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou was stricken with famine. Gao Kaidao offered grain for relief.

sentences.zh: 李藝遣老弱詣開道就食，開道皆厚遇之。

translations.literal: Li Yi sent the old and weak to Kaidao for food; Kaidao treated them all generously.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi sent the old and weak to Kaidao to be fed; Kaidao treated them all handsomely.

sentences.zh: 藝喜，於是發民三千人，車數百乘，驢馬千餘匹，往受粟。

translations.literal: Yi was pleased and therefore sent out three thousand people, several hundred carts, and more than a thousand donkeys and horses to receive grain.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was pleased and sent three thousand people, several hundred carts, and more than a thousand donkeys and horses to collect the grain.

sentences.zh: 開道悉留之，告絕於藝。

translations.literal: Kaidao kept them all and broke off relations with Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Kaidao kept them all and cut Yi off.

sentences.zh: 復稱燕王，北連突厥，南與劉黑闥相結，引兵攻易州，不克，大掠而去。

translations.literal: He again styled himself King of Yan, allied north with the Turks and south with Liu Heita, led troops to attack Yizhou, failed to take it, and departed after great plunder.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself King of Yan again, linked north with the Turks and south with Liu Heita, marched on Yizhou, failed to take it, and withdrew after a great sack.

sentences.zh: 又遣其將謝稜詐降於藝，請兵授接，藝出兵應之。

translations.literal: He also sent his general Xie Ling to feign surrender to Yi, asking for troops to link up; Yi marched out to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent his general Xie Ling to feign surrender to Yi and ask for troops to join him; Yi marched out to meet the ruse.

sentences.zh: 將至懷戎，稜襲擊破之。

translations.literal: When they were about to reach Huairou, Ling struck in a surprise attack and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: Near Huairou, Ling fell on them in a surprise attack and smashed them.

sentences.zh: 開道與突厥連兵數入為寇，恆、定、幽、易咸被其患。

translations.literal: Kaidao joined forces with the Turks and repeatedly raided in—Heng, Ding, You, and Yi all suffered from them.
translations.idiomatic: Kaidao and the Turks raided again and again; Heng, Ding, You, and Yi all suffered.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙卯，劉黑闥陷冀州，殺刺史麴稜。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yimao, Liu Heita took Jizhou and killed prefect Qu Ling.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yimao, Liu Heita took Jizhou and killed prefect Qu Ling.

sentences.zh: 黑闥既破淮安王神通，移書趙、魏，故竇建德將卒爭殺唐官吏以應黑闥。

translations.literal: After Heita had defeated Prince of Huai'an Shentong, he sent letters to Zhao and Wei; former Dou Jiande's officers and soldiers competed to kill Tang officials in response to Heita.
translations.idiomatic: After Heita broke Prince of Huai'an Shentong, he sent letters through Zhao and Wei; Dou Jiande's old officers and men vied to kill Tang officials and rally to Heita.

sentences.zh: 庚申，遣右屯衛大將軍義安王孝常將兵討黑闥。

translations.literal: On gengshen, the Right Stationed Guard General, Prince of Yi'an Xiaochang, was dispatched with troops to attack Heita.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Right Stationed Guard General Prince of Yi'an Xiaochang was sent with an army against Heita.

sentences.zh: 黑闥將兵數萬進逼宗城，黎州總管李世勣先屯宗城，棄城走保洺州。

translations.literal: Heita led tens of thousands of troops pressing on Zongcheng. Lizhou governor-general Li Shiji had earlier encamped at Zongcheng; he abandoned the city and fled to hold Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Heita advanced on Zongcheng with tens of thousands of men. Lizhou governor-general Li Shiji, who had been holding Zongcheng, abandoned it and fled to Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 甲子，黑闥追擊世勣等，破之，殺步卒五千人，世勣僅以身免。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Heita pursued Li Shiji and the others, defeated them, killed five thousand foot soldiers; Shiji escaped with his life alone.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Heita chased Li Shiji and the rest, broke them, and killed five thousand foot soldiers; Shiji alone got away.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，洺州土豪翻城應黑闥。

translations.literal: On bingyin, local strongmen of Mozhou turned the city in response to Heita.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Mozhou's local strongmen opened the city to Heita.

sentences.zh: 黑闥築壇於城東南，告天及祭竇建德而後入；

translations.literal: Heita built an altar southeast of the city, announced to Heaven and sacrificed to Dou Jiande, and only then entered;
translations.idiomatic: Heita raised an altar southeast of the city, announced his cause to Heaven, and sacrificed to Dou Jiande before he entered;

sentences.zh: 後旬日，引兵攻拔相州，執刺史房晃，右武衛將軍張士貴潰圍走。

translations.literal: ten days later he led troops to attack and take Xiangzhou, seized prefect Fang Huang; Right Martial Guard General Zhang Shigui broke out of the siege and fled.
translations.idiomatic: ten days on he marched on Xiangzhou, took it, and seized prefect Fang Huang; Right Martial Guard General Zhang Shigui broke out and fled.

sentences.zh: 黑闥南取黎、衛二州，半歲之間，盡復建德舊境。

translations.literal: Heita took Li and Wei prefectures to the south; within half a year he had fully restored Jiande's old territory.
translations.idiomatic: Heita swept south through Li and Wei; within half a year he had restored all of Jiande's old domain.

sentences.zh: 又遣使北連突厥，頡利可汗遣俟斤宋邪那帥胡騎從之。

translations.literal: He also sent envoys north to ally with the Turks; Khan Jieli sent yabghu Song Xiena with Turkic cavalry to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent envoys north to the Turks; Khan Jieli dispatched yabghu Song Xiena at the head of Turkic horse to join him.

sentences.zh: 右武衛將軍秦武通、洺州刺史陳君賓、永寧令程名振皆自河北遁歸長安。

translations.literal: Right Martial Guard General Qin Wutong, Mozhou prefect Chen Junbin, and Yongning magistrate Cheng Mingzhen all fled from Hebei back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Right Martial Guard General Qin Wutong, Mozhou prefect Chen Junbin, and Yongning magistrate Cheng Mingzhen all fled Hebei for Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，命秦王世民、齊王元吉討黑闥。

translations.literal: On dingmao, the Prince of Qin Shimin and Prince of Qi Yuanji were ordered to attack Heita.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Prince of Qin Shimin and Prince of Qi Yuanji were ordered to crush Heita.

sentences.zh: 昆彌遣使內附。

translations.literal: Kunming sent envoys to submit internally.
translations.idiomatic: Kunming sent envoys to submit.

sentences.zh: 昆彌，即漢之昆明也。

translations.literal: Kunming—that is, the Kunming of Han times.
translations.idiomatic: Kunming—the Kunming people of Han times.

sentences.zh: 巂州治中吉駐緯通南寧，至其國說之，遂來降。

translations.literal: Ji Wei, assistant prefect of Xi Prefecture, went by way of Nanning to their state and persuaded them; they then came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Wei, assistant prefect of Xi Prefecture, traveled through Nanning to their country and won them over; they then submitted.

sentences.zh: 己巳，劉黑闥陷邢州、趙州；

translations.literal: On jisi, Liu Heita took Xingzhou and Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jisi, Liu Heita captured Xingzhou and Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 庚午，陷魏州，殺總管潘道毅；

translations.literal: On gengwu, he took Weizhou and killed regional commander Pan Daoyi.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengwu, he took Weizhou and killed regional commander Pan Daoyi.

sentences.zh: 辛未，陷莘州。

translations.literal: On xinwei, he took Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinwei, he captured Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 壬申，徙宋王元嘉為徐王。

translations.literal: On renshen, Prince of Song Yuanjia was transferred to be Prince of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renshen, Prince Yuanjia of Song was re-designated Prince of Xu.
